bills.summary: Would make it a crime for a library to let a kid look up anything obscene online

bills.description: The pharmacy tech was taught to guess hard words from the first letter and the context. The label says hydroxyzine. {name} walks out with hydralazine, and their blood pressure bottoms out on the highway an hour later.

bills.description: The church potluck in town is hosted by a homeschool co-op of thirty families. The state stopped asking them for anything, vaccine records included. One of the toddlers has a rash. Ten days later, so does most of the van.

A thirteen-year-old, out of school since the state stopped checking, is driving the family hay truck on the county road. He takes the curve wide. {name} is in the passenger seat of the van and takes the windshield.

The state pays for its new test and not the SAT, so the high school traded its free SAT day for the new one. The motel is full of families driving to the region's last SAT site, and the party sleeps at a rest area.
bills.summary: Allows students to take the fake SAT

bills.description: {name} does a drag number at the bar's open-mic night, fully clothed, as they have in four states. A deputy in the back decides it's obscene. The charge is a felony, and the bond hearing isn't until Monday.

The fire hall is a polling place today, and the man arguing over a yard sign in line has brought his pistol inside, legally. He fires twice. {name}, filling the party's water jugs at the spigot by the door, is hit in the hip.
bills.summary: Allows you to bring a gun to a polling place

A third grader is sent home for wearing cat ears to school. Her mother, the only mechanic in town, leaves the van up on the lift to go get her and doesn't come back that day. The part goes in on Monday.

Sued over the books it pulled, the county voted to close the library rather than put them back. The food pantry in the basement closed with it. The party had planned to restock there and stretches what it has to the next state.

Health class may now mention contraception only as something that fails. The seventeen-year-old cashier at the truck stop is pregnant for the second time. When she collapses behind the counter, the party waits with her for the ambulance and minds the store.

bills.summary: Requires schools to disclose every book they have online, making it easier for gadflies to ban books

bills.summary: Requires schools to show pro-life propaganda

bills.description: The sixteen-year-old working the campground office was homeschooled by a parent who left school in seventh grade. She can't read the reservation screen well enough to see that the party's site was booked twice. The party drives on in the dark.
bills.summary: Makes it so homeschool parents don't have to have graduated high school

bills.description: One of the party is assigned Beloved for an online class. The library's copy is in the restricted room, which requires a county card, which requires proof of local address. The bookstore two towns over has a copy.
bills.summary: Require libraries have an age restricted section with Beloved in it

bills.summary: Bans schools from addressing students as anything but the name on the birth certificate

The girl in the trailer behind the campground hasn't been seen in two years; homeschooling families no longer report anything. The party notices the padlock is on the outside of her door and calls it in. The deputies take the rest of the day.

The district spent its maintenance budget on a camera in every room of every school. The high school gym is still the county's flood shelter, and its roof still leaks. The party spends the flood night there, on camera. The food is soaked by morning.

The party's youngest took the new test because the state counts it for scholarships. The university in Oregon doesn't count it at all. The admission falls through, and the housing deposit goes with it.

The state police dropped their bias and de-escalation training, which the new law counts as a divisive concept. {name} is pulled over for a taillight. The trooper grabs their arm before they've finished reaching for the glovebox, and the shoulder dislocates on the door frame.

{name} is thirty-four weeks pregnant and has never had an ultrasound; the only pregnancy class they ever took covered fetal fingerprints, not the word prenatal. It's placenta previa. The bleeding starts on a ranch road outside Casper.

The motel clerk skipped her flu shot this year, like the radio said to. She hands over the room keys between coughs. The whole party spends the next four days shivering in that room with the heat on high.

{name} shares a pancake-house booth with a toddler who has a fever and a rash. Ten days later {name} has measles. Three days after that, measles pneumonia.
It is the state's first diphtheria case in decades, and {name} sat next to it on the airport shuttle. A gray membrane spreads across the back of their throat. The antitoxin has to be flown in.

A bat gets into {name}'s motel room overnight. The ER cleans the scratch but won't start the rabies shots; offering a vaccine is now a crime here. The nearest hospital across the state line is hours away.
bills.summary: Create criminal penalties for offering vaccines

bills.description: {name} had a kidney transplant three years ago and can't get live vaccines; they rely on the kids around them having theirs. A kindergarten field trip at the science museum has chickenpox. {name} spends a week on IV antivirals.
{name} is twelve weeks pregnant and never had rubella. A cousin's kid at the family reunion has a rash that everyone says is nothing. It is rubella, and twelve weeks is the worst possible time.
{name}'s physical therapist no longer has to be vaccinated and doesn't mention the cough. Two weeks of knee rehab become two weeks of COVID, followed by four more weeks of knee rehab.
Not the daycare, not the hospital, not the summer camp, not the nursing home. Measles moves through all four, then through the motel where the party stops for the night.
The children's hospital is full of measles cases, and so is the regional ER. The urgent care where the party needs a prescription refilled has a fourteen-hour wait and a line out the door.
The ER doctor who stitches {name}'s forehead is coughing behind a loose mask and has never had a whooping cough booster. Three weeks later {name} is coughing hard enough to crack a rib.

The motel clerk skipped her flu shot this year, like the radio said to. She hands over the room keys between coughs. The whole party spends the next four days shivering in that room with the heat on high.
bills.sponsor: Committee on Health and Human Services

bills.description: The county library spent the month pulling four hundred titles for review, and the librarian quit. The building is closed. The free wifi, the printer and the forms the party needed are behind a locked door.
bills.summary: Makes it easier to ban library books

bills.description: Two kids in the motel hot tub have puffy cheeks, and {name} shares the water with them. Mumps arrives eighteen days later. When the swelling goes down, the hearing in {name}'s left ear does not come back.
The state now tells parents, in writing, that opting out is an option. Plenty of them take it. Whooping cough goes from the elementary school to the grocery store to the van.
The scenic railway ride the party booked months ago, and drove ninety miles out of the way for, is cancelled: mumps among the crew. There is no new date. The party drives the ninety miles back.

{name} catches measles from a kid in line at a gas station and recovers in two weeks. Then the immune amnesia sets in. By fall, a routine sinus infection has become pneumonia.

Every pint donated in the state now needs a vaccination label and its own shelf. The blood center cancels its rural drives to keep up. The hospital on the route postpones scheduled surgery for a month, including the hernia repair the party drove here for.
bills.summary: Requires blood from people who got vaccinated to be separately labeled and stored

bills.description: {name} needs dialysis three times a week, wherever the van happens to be. The center in Peoria no longer requires its staff to be vaccinated. COVID is on the unit by Monday, and {name} is admitted by Thursday.

After a fender-bender, all five get checked out at the county hospital. Nobody is hurt. The flu outbreak on the floor, spread by staff who can't be required to get the shot, sends them all back two days later.
bills.summary: Bans health care programs from requiring vaccination

{name}'s femur snaps in a fall at a scenic overlook. Surgery needs blood. Much of the state's donor pool is now barred from giving, and the hospital has four units of O-negative for three patients. {name} is the fourth.
bills.summary: Bans people who got the COVID vaccine from donating blood

bills.description: Blood banks now run two inventories and two sets of trucks. The rural hospital ahead lost its delivery route and stopped taking trauma. After a minor crash, the party is sent ninety minutes past it to be seen.
bills.summary: Segregate COVID vaccinated blood in blood banks

bills.description: A measles outbreak that started in one unvaccinated community reaches a truck stop on the interstate. The party ate there. Five fevers, five rashes, one van.

The summer camp the party is driving a niece to can no longer ask for shot records. Chickenpox is in two cabins, and the camp sends everyone home. The party turns around and drives her back the way they came.
bills.summary: Making it harder to require immunization

bills.description: {name} is seventy-three and has a heart condition. Nobody on the senior center bus has to be vaccinated, including the driver. {name} rides it to the pharmacy and comes home with COVID that settles into their lungs.
The restaurant can't require its staff to be vaccinated, and the line cook with influenza can't afford a sick day. He makes the party's dinner.

Whooping cough closes both daycares in the parish. The motel's housekeepers stay home with their kids, the motel stops renting rooms it can't clean, and the party spends two nights in the van at a boat launch.
{name} books a bunk in a twelve-bed hostel dorm. Vaccination used to be the house rule; now it isn't allowed to be. Eight of the twelve have COVID by morning, including {name}.
The whale-watching boat is packed, and nobody had to show a vaccine card to board. By the time a whale surfaces, half the passengers are coughing. A week later, so is the party.

{name} takes immunosuppressants for a transplant and used to choose where to go by the sign on the door. No door has that sign now. {name} catches COVID at a museum and spends ten days in the hospital.
bills.summary: Ban on requiring COVID vaccine for entry into anywhere

bills.description: Every meat label in the state now needs a vaccination audit. The local processor can't afford one and closes. The farm stand where the party planned to restock has a hand-lettered sign: no meat until further notice.
bills.summary: Requires food companies to disclose vaccinated meat

bills.description: Two kids at the water park have a cough and red eyes, and their family's exemption forms are in order. The party spent all afternoon on the same pool deck. Measles reaches the van eleven days later.
{name} picks up a day of substitute teaching to cover gas. Eleven of the twenty-two third graders are out sick, and two of the ones who came in are flushed and spotty. Nine days later, so is {name}.

The island ferry cancels sailings for a week: the crew has COVID and the state can't require the replacements to be vaccinated either. The party's motel on the island is paid for. The party is on the mainland.
bills.summary: Ban on any COVID vaccination requirements

bills.description: Chickenpox closes the county's daycares, and the auto shop's only mechanic stays home with his twins. The van's new alternator sits in a box on the counter for five days.
The surgical nurse who preps {name} for a gallbladder operation is unvaccinated and, as of that morning, coughing. The incision heals in a week. The COVID pneumonia takes three.

{name} has severe asthma and was due for a COVID shot. No pharmacy in Mississippi can give one now. {name} catches the virus at a Jackson gas station and spends three nights in a hospital bed on a nebulizer.

Mississippi used to have one of the highest school vaccination rates in the country. Now a family with three spotty kids is staying down the hall at the motel. The party shares an ice machine with them. Measles follows.

Rabies turns up in a herd of unvaccinated cattle outside town. The state vet quarantines the farm roads, including the one the party is on, and wants to interview anyone who stopped at the roadside milk stand. The party did.
A farm dog that by law can't have had a rabies shot bites {name} on the calf. The dog is put down and tested. Positive. The ER has to order the immune globulin from Memphis.
{name} is seven months pregnant and catches measles at a church potluck. Labor starts three weeks early, in an isolation room, with the staff in respirators.

The state's investigation subpoenas every pharmacy's vaccine records. Two rural pharmacies decide it's simpler to stop giving shots, and one decides it's simpler to close. The party drives ninety miles out of the way for a refill.

The Billings pharmacy pulled its COVID doses off the shelf the day the law took effect. {name}, sixty-eight with a bad heart, was booked for that afternoon. They catch COVID in a crowded casino and spend five days in the cardiac unit.
bills.summary: Bans all mRNA vaccines in MT

bills.description: Bird flu is moving through the valley's dairy herds, and the vaccine the state vet wanted is mRNA, so it can't be used. Herds are quarantined and milk is dumped. The creamery where the party planned to restock is empty by ten.
bills.summary: Ban on mRNA vaccines for livestock

bills.description: {name} sleeps on a friend's dorm floor during a campus mumps outbreak. The swelling starts at the jaw. Then it reaches the lining of the brain: mumps meningitis, nine days in a Durham hospital.

The exemption is now one line and a signature. In one elementary school, a third of the parents sign it. Whooping cough runs through the school, then the soccer tournament, then the hotel where the party took the last room.
bills.summary: Make it easier to get out of vaccination requirements

bills.description: The oncology ward can no longer assign nurses by vaccination status; that would be discrimination. {name}, halfway through chemo, gets the nurse with the flu.
bills.summary: Grants unvaccinated people civil rights protections

bills.description: {name} books a bunk in a twelve-bed hostel dorm. Vaccination used to be the house rule; now it isn't allowed to be. Eight of the twelve have COVID by morning, including {name}.
A legislative commission on a 1967 naval attack holds its hearing at the statehouse. The party stops in Concord to file a form and finds the office closed for the day and every parking space taken.

Mumps runs through a college town on the route. The health department asks everyone who was at Saturday's game to get a booster and stay out of crowds for a week. The party was at the game. Six nights in a motel.

The association that bulk-bought every child's vaccines in the state is gone. Pediatricians now buy doses retail and bill families. A cousin's two-month shots, picked up on the way through, cost the party a week of groceries.
The elementary school can't host its flu clinic anymore. The kids get the flu instead and pass it to the clerk at the general store, who passes it to {name}. It becomes pneumonia.
bills.summary: Ban on vaccination clinics at schools

bills.description: The scenic railway ride the party booked months ago, and drove ninety miles out of the way for, is cancelled: mumps among the crew. There is no new date. The party drives the ninety miles back.
Measles comes up from a school in the valley and settles into the ski lodge. The party stayed two nights. The lodge's guest list goes to the health department, and the rash comes to the van.

Mumps runs through a college town on the route. The health department asks everyone who was at Saturday's game to get a booster and stay out of crowds for a week. The party was at the game. Six nights in a motel.
{name} is twelve weeks pregnant and never had rubella. A cousin's kid at the family reunion has a rash that everyone says is nothing. It is rubella, and twelve weeks is the worst possible time.

A man fires a rifle, legal again under the narrower definition, through the windows of a crowded thruway rest stop. The party is near the glass. None of them is shot. None of them walks out without stitches.
The only pharmacy in town has a sign taped to the door: closed, staff out with COVID. The party's insulin refill is two counties away, in the wrong direction.
COVID closes the school district for two weeks. The party's cousin is a single parent and an ER nurse who can't take the time off. The party stays to watch her kids.
bills.summary: Ban schools from requiring COVID vaccines

bills.description: {name} is thirty weeks pregnant, and no one in New York can give them a COVID shot now. They catch it at a rest stop. The fever brings on labor, ten weeks early, in a hospital in Binghamton.
The party gives a ride to a teacher whose car died outside Albany. She has spent the week in a classroom with measles and doesn't know it yet. Neither does the party.
COVID takes out the staff at three thruway service plazas in one week, and the state can't require the replacements to be vaccinated either. The plazas close. The van runs out of gas outside Utica.
bills.summary: Ban government from requiring COVID vaccination

bills.description: The comedy club can't ask for vaccine cards. Two hundred people laugh in a basement for ninety minutes. The party is among the forty who leave with COVID.
A measles outbreak that started in one unvaccinated community reaches a truck stop on the interstate. The party ate there. Five fevers, five rashes, one van.
In a Columbus ER waiting room, {name} sits beside an infant with a cough and a rash. Ten days later {name} has measles. Weeks after the rash fades, the encephalitis the doctors called rare arrives.
The state's campaign against flu shots has worked. The van's axle breaks outside Enid, and three of the county tow company's four drivers are home with the flu. The wait for a truck is two days.
Half the high school football team has COVID and plays anyway. The party sits in the home bleachers for the Friday game. By Saturday morning, there are five sore throats in the van.

{name} has sickle cell disease and needs regular transfusions. The supplier now ships unvaccinated blood at a premium, and the hospital rations the rest. {name}'s transfusion is pushed back two weeks. The pain crisis comes in one.
The surgical nurse who preps {name} for a gallbladder operation is unvaccinated and, as of that morning, coughing. The incision heals in a week. The COVID pneumonia takes three.
{name} has COPD and asks about the pneumonia shot. The doctor is now required to talk them out of it, and is thorough. Three weeks later, pneumococcal pneumonia puts {name} on a ventilator in Tulsa.
Nearly every cow in the state got a vaccine at some point, so nearly every steak is now banned. The supermarket meat case holds a little bison, priced like jewelry. The party's rations shrink.
Under the amendment, no school, camp or employer can ask. Measles closes the Route 66 museum, the diner across the street and the motel next door. The party's overnight in Clinton becomes a week.
{name} is on chemotherapy and was due for a COVID booster this month. No pharmacy in the state is allowed to stock it. A cough picked up at a gas station becomes a week on oxygen.
Whooping cough at a rodeo in Guymon. The party sat two rows behind the grandfather who brought it, and coughs its way through the next three states.

A whooping cough case in the next motel room means a course of preventive antibiotics for everyone on the floor. The county health department has a six-hour line. The party spends the day in it, and another night in the motel.
{name} cuts a hand pulling a stranger out of a wreck on I-40. The stranger has hepatitis B, and {name} never got the shots as a kid. Six months later, the infection is chronic.
The family that runs the roadside motel has whooping cough and keeps the office open anyway. The party checks in for two nights. The coughing lasts considerably longer.

A COVID wave knocks out a third of the staff at the state's largest hospital. Non-urgent appointments are cancelled, including the specialist visit the party drove four days to make.

The high school's new vaccine-refusal assembly works. Measles closes the school, then the public pool, then the motel next door, which won't take guests from the exposure zone. That includes the party.
bills.summary: Encourages students to not get vaccinated

bills.description: {name} breaks a wrist and lands in a Harrisburg ER, where a coughing, unvaccinated tech has a constitutional right to keep working. It's the flu. With {name}'s asthma, it becomes pneumonia.
bills.summary: Constitutional right to not get vaccinated

bills.description: Bird flu hits the egg farms in Lancaster County. The mRNA poultry vaccine the farmers hoped for is illegal here. Millions of hens are culled, and the eggs the party planned to stock up on are gone from every shelf.

{name} hemorrhages after giving birth in Scranton. The hospital has blood, but the new consent form asks which kind {name} would prefer, and {name} is past answering questions. Twenty minutes go to the paperwork.
A COVID wave knocks out a third of the staff at the state's largest hospital. Non-urgent appointments are cancelled, including the specialist visit the party drove four days to make.
To keep selling in the state, the chicken farm stopped vaccinating its flock against salmonella. The party's rest-stop chicken sandwiches deliver it.
bills.summary: Requiring meat come from unvaccinated animals

bills.description: {name} has been on the kidney transplant list for three years. A match comes in from a donor who was vaccinated. The new segregation paperwork takes longer than a kidney keeps.
bills.summary: Requring vaccinated people's blood and organs be segregated

bills.description: Farms that vaccinate their cattle lose the state-grown label, and the farmers market drops them. The market where the party planned to restock is down to two stalls: honey and boiled peanuts.
bills.summary: Bans vaccinated meat from getting in-state designation

bills.description: {name} is on a state hospital's transplant ward. Turning away an unvaccinated visitor could now cost the state a lawsuit, so nobody tries. The visitor in the next room's doorway has measles.
bills.summary: Allow unvaccinated people to sue the state for damages arising from getting denied services

Tennessee records its first paralytic polio case in decades, an unvaccinated eight-year-old who swam at the same lake as {name}. By Tuesday {name} can't lift their left leg.

With no federal schedule to point to, the state's insurers stop covering shots they aren't sure they have to. The party's tetanus boosters, needed after a rusty nail at a campsite, come out of the grocery budget.

{name} is in a Memphis trial of a personalized mRNA vaccine against their melanoma. The trial is now illegal in Tennessee. It moves to another state, and {name} has to follow it between doses, if a slot opens.

bills.description: The party stops for gas in Seminole. The cashier's daughter is coloring behind the counter, flushed, with spots along her hairline. Everyone in the van paid inside.

Flood season. The National Guard unit sent to sandbag the river has a flu outbreak and stands down for a week. The bridge goes under. The detour takes two days.
bills.summary: Eliminates vaccination requirements for national guard

bills.description: {name}'s doctor in Austin used to give the COVID shot in the office. That shot is illegal now, and the only other kind is back-ordered for months. {name} catches COVID at a rodeo; their diabetes makes it a five-day hospital stay.

bills.summary: Allow pharmacists to refuse to give vaccines

{name}'s doctor at the Dallas urgent care has measles and doesn't know it yet. {name} leaves with an antibiotic prescription and, ten days later, the measles.
Measles at the Zion visitor center. The park closes its shuttle and its lodge for contact tracing. The party's campsite, booked eight months ago, is cancelled by text message.

bills.description: The county 4-H fair has prize hogs, funnel cakes and, in the poultry barn, a nine-year-old with measles. The party walked through every barn.

Half the students at the private academy across from the motel were never vaccinated. {name} buys ice cream at the stand where their parents line up after pickup. Ten days later: fever, cough, a rash from the hairline down.
bills.summary: Exempts private schools from vaccination requirements

bills.description: Flu season, and every exemption was granted. The pharmacy, the urgent care and the grocery store all close early for lack of staff. The party loses two days waiting for groceries and a prescription.

The party stops to take a cousin's foster toddler for the weekend. Nobody in the foster home has to be vaccinated now, and the other kids have chickenpox. The toddler, on steroids for asthma, is admitted. The weekend becomes nine days.
bills.summary: Eliminate vaccination requirements for foster parents

Traffickers run pistols up I-40, and state police can no longer help the ATF trace them. One of those pistols is pointed at {name} at a gas station in Russellville. They hand over the wallet and get hit anyway.
bills.summary: Ban state from working with ATF to enforce gun laws

bills.description: {name}'s brother-in-law has a domestic violence conviction, so federal law bars him from owning a gun. Nobody in Arkansas will enforce that now. He brings it to the family cookout, and {name} steps between him and their sister.
bills.summary: Ban on state enforcing federal gun laws

bills.description: Arizona stopped enforcing federal water rules, so the copper mine upstream stopped treating its runoff. The campground well in Globe tests high for arsenic. The party has been drinking from it for three days.
bills.summary: Allows nullification of federal environmental laws

bills.description: State troopers and federal agents now share the checkpoint south of Tucson, and each ignores the other's rules. The party is searched by both, twice, and released at dusk.
bills.summary: Declaration it'll ignore federal laws it doesn't like

bills.description: Indiana decided OSHA was unconstitutional, and the grain elevator outside Lafayette dropped its bin-entry rules. {name}, taking a day's work for gas money, goes in without a harness to break up a crust. The corn gives way.
bills.summary: Allows state to ignore federal actions it deems unconstitutional

bills.description: The legislature has declared the state supreme court's order void. The county judge in Frankfort is no longer sure which orders count, including the one releasing the party's impounded van. It sits in the lot another week.
bills.summary: Declaring a state supreme court order regarding impeachment unconstitutional

bills.description: {name} arrives at the ER in Pikeville with appendicitis and no insurance. The hospital no longer considers the federal law requiring it to treat them binding in Kentucky. They're handed a list of clinics.
bills.summary: Allows Kentucky to nullify federal laws

bills.description: The coal company stopped following federal mine safety rules once Kentucky said it could. Nobody inspected the slurry pond above the road. When it gives way, the van is downstream, and the party wades out through black sludge.
Missouri opted out of the federal hours-of-service rule for truckers. The semi jackknifed across I-70 near Columbia was on its driver's twenty-second hour. The interstate is closed until dark.
bills.summary: Allows state to opt out of federal regulations

bills.description: Oklahoma deems the EPA's refinery emissions rules unconstitutional and stops enforcing them. The refinery in Ponca City flares all night. {name}, who has asthma, spends it in the ER on a nebulizer.
bills.summary: Allows state to declare federal actions unconstitutional

bills.description: Nobody in Oklahoma enforces the federal rules on underground fuel tanks now. The truck stop pump outside Oklahoma City puts water in the van's tank. It stalls on the on-ramp, and the tow takes the afternoon.

A straw buyer in Philadelphia buys twelve pistols in a week. Federal agents know, and are not allowed to act on it here. One ends up with the teenager who carjacks {name} at a red light in Kensington and fires when they hesitate.
bills.summary: Ban any federal enforcement of gun laws

bills.description: Tennessee nullified the ADA as federal overreach. The motel in Jackson pulled out its ramp and turns away the party member who uses a wheelchair. The next motel that can take them is in Memphis.
bills.summary: Allows state to nullify federal laws

bills.description: The state declared federal meat inspection rules void. The brisket at a roadside stand came from a plant nobody checks anymore. {name} has E. coli by morning, and by the weekend their kidneys are struggling.
bills.summary: Allows state to nullify federal laws that it doesn't like

bills.description: Tennessee nullified the federal rules on workplace heat. {name} takes a warehouse shift in Memphis for gas money: no water breaks, heat index 106. They collapse on the loading dock in the fourth hour.

West Virginia no longer honors the Supreme Court's right-to-counsel ruling. {name}, arrested after a fender-bender in Beckley, is arraigned without a lawyer and pleads to something they didn't do. Ninety days.
bills.summary: Allows state to nullify Supreme Court decisions that it doesn't like

bills.description: Federal agents can't inspect the gun shop in Martinsburg anymore, and its off-the-books sales go up I-81 by the carload. A shooting outside Hagerstown closes the interstate for the afternoon.
bills.summary: Ban federal enforcement of gun laws

bills.description: The treasurer put part of the state's reserves into crypto and calls the 60 percent loss a long-term hold. In the short term, Alabama is delaying tax refunds. The one a party member earned at a summer job in Mobile is now expected in spring.
bills.summary: Authorizing state treasurer to invest in crypto

bills.description: A text says the van owes an unpaid toll and links to a state payment page that takes Bitcoin. It looks real, because the state really does take Bitcoin now. The money cannot be reversed.
bills.summary: Let state accept payments in crypto

bills.description: Crypto gains in Alabama are tax-free now. Wages are not. One of the party picks up two days of farm work outside Dothan, and the state takes its share of the pay, then takes it again at the grocery register.
{name} is camping on public land behind a private gun range. The berm was never raised; no one could be sued over it anymore. A round clears it and goes through the tent.
bills.summary: Limiting liability of gun range owners

bills.description: {name}'s diabetes was managed through a county program the department paid for: test strips, and a nurse who called every Friday. The nurse's number is disconnected. Their blood sugar reads 410 at an urgent care in Pine Bluff.

The efficiency office halved the restaurant inspection staff and announced the savings. The diner off exit 42 hasn't seen an inspector in fourteen months. Everyone orders the chicken salad. Everyone is sick by midnight.
A foursome finishes eighteen holes and two coolers of their own beer, with no bartender to cut anyone off. Their pickup leaves the club lot at four. {name} is in the crosswalk.

The corporate tax cut was balanced partly by trimming weights-and-measures inspectors. The pump at the party's last fill-up has been shorting every customer for months, and nobody has checked it. Neither did the party.
The bitcoin mine outside town draws more power than the town does and pays no tax on it. On a 114-degree afternoon the utility sheds load. The motel's air conditioning is the first thing to go.
bills.summary: Bars taxes on running bitcoin mines

bills.summary: Requires state to invest in crypto

bills.summary: Asking the state treasurer to invest in BItcoin

The law makes Iowa buy crypto on a fixed schedule, and traders know the schedule. They buy the day before and sell to the state the day after. Campground fees at state parks go up to cover it. The party pays at the gate.

The call comes from the county sheriff's real number: a missed jury summons, a fine payable at the crypto kiosk in the gas station. The kiosk takes the party's cash. The sheriff's office has never heard of any of it.

The state now routes park and permit payments through a crypto processor. The processor froze withdrawals on Friday. The ranger station cannot sell a camping pass any other way, and the gate stays down until further notice.

The new data center pumps from the same aquifer as the town, and it got the tax break and the water rights first. The town's wells are dropping. The campground shuts off its taps at noon on a 98-degree day.

The estate tax now starts at twelve million, which covers a few hundred families and no one in this van. The shortfall cut lifeguards at state park beaches. {name} is caught in a Lake Michigan rip current beside an empty chair.

bills.description: A bat gets into the motel room overnight and {name} wakes up with a bite on their hand. The state program that paid for rabies shots for people who couldn't was cut to make room for the estate tax break. The clock is running.

The heirs keep all of it now. The party's receipts from one day on the road include sales tax on the motel, the gas, the groceries and a gas-station sandwich. Together they come to more than the estate paid.
The income tax stays flat, so the counties lean on fees, and the county clinic now charges just to be seen. {name} decides the cough can wait. By Saturday it is pneumonia.

The sales tax is now high enough to replace the income tax, and it covers groceries and gas. The resupply stop in Terre Haute buys about four-fifths of what it would have bought one state back.
bills.summary: Replaces income tax with sales tax

bills.description: {name}'s sister in Fort Wayne has two kids and a husband who has already broken her wrist once. Without his consent or proof of fault a judge will accept, she cannot divorce him. {name} goes to pick her up. He is home.
bills.summary: Eliminates no fault divorce for parents

bills.description: The party's emergency money came from a retirement account one of them cashed out before the trip. The plan's new crypto option was the one HR recommended. It is worth less than half of what it was.

Lawmakers can now lobby the agencies whose budgets they write. A paving company hires one, and wins the highway contract. The new asphalt is already coming apart, and the van loses a day to the patching.
bills.summary: Allow state lawmakers to serve as lobbyists to state agencies

bills.description: A wallet nobody can trace gave the maximum to every member of the utilities committee. The committee approved the rate increase. The motel passes it along as an energy surcharge, and so does every gas station on the route.

{name} breaks a wrist on the rocks at the beach. The town's ambulance went private after the local aid cuts that paid for the capital gains break, and the private one is forty minutes out.

The bitcoin stake fell 40 percent, and the shortfall closed the community hospital's maternity unit. {name} is thirty-six weeks pregnant. They deliver on the shoulder of Route 2, and keep bleeding after the baby is out.

The refinery in southwest Detroit flares for three days straight, and the state is no longer allowed to set a limit tighter than Washington's, which was just rolled back. The motel is a mile downwind. Everyone is coughing by the second night.
bills.summary: Prohibit state from regulating pollution more stringently than the federal government

bills.description: The party kept its travel fund in an app a man at the campground swore by, a crypto exchange the state is now barred from licensing or auditing. Withdrawals were paused this morning. Customer support is a chatbot.

The emergency order closed gyms, bars and churches during the outbreak, but not the indoor gun range, which the law protects. The party shoots a few rounds in a poorly ventilated room with forty strangers. Two days later, everyone has a fever.
bills.summary: Keeping gun ranges open during emergencies

The towing industry hires two lawmakers the week they leave office, and the predatory-towing bill never gets a hearing. The van is towed from a motel lot at 3 a.m. The impound lot opens Tuesday.
bills.summary: Make it easier for lawmakers to work as lobbyists

bills.description: A cold snap hits, the crypto mines keep running at full load, and the utility orders rolling blackouts. The motel goes dark at eighteen below. The party sleeps in coats, in the van, with the engine running.
bills.summary: Eliminates requirement that crypto not waste energy

bills.description: The crypto loss came out of human services, and the regional crisis beds went first. {name}, deep in a depressive episode and no longer safe alone, spends three days on a gurney in an ER hallway waiting for a bed four hours away.
The state efficiency office eliminated the overnight snowplow shift as redundant. At 5 a.m. the van meets black ice on an untreated grade. {name}'s collarbone meets the door frame.

With no corporate income tax coming in, the highway patrol froze hiring. The van breaks down after dark on I-70 and nobody comes. After three hours {name} walks along the shoulder toward the next exit. A truck's mirror finds them first.

The capital gains cut was offset by trimming commercial truck inspections. A log truck with brakes nobody checked runs out of road on a downgrade and clips the van. Everyone walks away. Not everyone walks well.

The treasurer has to keep buying Bitcoin whatever the price, and this month the price is bad. The state's prescription assistance program stops enrolling to cover the gap. {name} can't afford the inhaler in Rolla and goes without, the week the wildfire smoke arrives.

The new bitcoin fund was held by a contractor whose wallet was drained overnight. The legislature's answer is a freeze on all nonessential spending, effective at noon. The state park where the party had a reservation closes at 12:01.
The used tire bought in Joplin separates at seventy miles an hour. The manufacturer knew about the defect. Under the new law, that barely matters. {name} has a broken wrist and no case.
bills.summary: Makes it harder to win a products liability lawsuit

bills.description: Medicaid payments to providers are being held for ninety days while the treasury absorbs its crypto loss. The dialysis center in town stopped taking new Medicaid patients. {name} misses one session, then a second.

A fortune can't be taxed until it is sold, and fortunes are rarely sold; their owners borrow against them cheaply. The party borrows gas money from a payday lender in Sedalia, which Missouri lets charge up to three-quarters of the loan in interest and fees.

Without an income tax, the state cut public health nurses first. Tuberculosis contact tracing is now one nurse covering four counties. The man coughing in the motel lobby last week was a case. {name} tests positive.
There is no longer a rule the county can enforce against the diner, the motel or the water park. The water park's pool has not been chlorinated in a week. Cryptosporidium does the rest.
bills.summary: Pretty much makes every business regulation null and void

bills.description: The crypto ATM at the truck stop takes the party's cash and prints a receipt for a wallet that does not exist. The operator's recorded message explains that, under state law, it is not liable for errors.
bills.summary: Seems to limit liability of crypto companies

bills.description: One of the party picks up three days of warehouse work in Hattiesburg, paid by paper check. No bank will cash it for a non-customer. The check casher down the road keeps a fifth.
Without an income tax, the state trimmed its hospital payments, and the hospital in this Delta county closed its emergency room. {name}'s chest pain gets the hour-long drive to Jackson instead.

Medicaid payments to providers are being held for ninety days while the treasury absorbs its crypto loss. The dialysis center in town stopped taking new Medicaid patients. {name} misses one session, then a second.

Western North Carolina still has mountain roads missing from the last hurricane. The money to rebuild them sits in a bitcoin reserve the state must hold, not spend. The party backtracks two days around a gap where the road used to be.
bills.summary: Require state to invest in Bitcoin

bills.description: Flood season arrived the same month the crypto position fell apart, and part of the emergency fund was in it. The sandbag line in the river town is half built. The motel's ground floor takes on water overnight, and so does the van.
bills.summary: Encourages the state to invest in crypto

bills.description: The crypto mine next to the motel runs four hundred cooling fans around the clock, and the town can no longer zone it out. Nobody in the party sleeps for two nights. On the third morning the driver nods off on US-2.
bills.summary: Requires commercial districts permit crypto mining

bills.description: The committee that oversees pipeline safety spent a long weekend at an oil company's hunting lodge. The inspection schedule was revised on the flight home. The pipeline under the highway leaks, and the road closes for a week of cleanup.
bills.summary: Legalizes taking gifts from lobbyists on junkets

bills.description: Nebraska's counties paid for roads and deputies with the inheritance tax. This one has stopped grading its gravel roads. The van sinks to the axles on a soft stretch and waits a day for a farmer with a tractor.

bills.summary: Encourages the state to invest in crypto

bills.description: The crypto mine in the old textile mill has not had a fire inspection since the law passed. It burns overnight. The smoke settles over the campground across the river before anyone thinks to wake it.
The efficiency office decided the state had more 911 dispatchers than it needed. When {name} collapses in a Turnpike service plaza, the call rings for four minutes before anyone picks up.
With a flat tax, the state made up the difference with tolls. The Turnpike, the Parkway and every bridge out of the state went up again. The party pays seven of them before lunch.

Without income tax revenue, the forestry division ran a crew short this summer. The fire near Ruidoso jumps the highway faster than anyone planned for. The party drives out through the smoke with the vents closed, which helps less than you would think.
The bitcoin purchase emptied the account that paid for rural road maintenance. The paved road to the next town is now a dirt road with a sign apologizing for it. It is monsoon season.

The estate tax is gone, and Albany made up part of it by cutting county health grants. The tick clinic in the Hudson Valley closed in the spring. {name} has a bullseye rash and a fever, and the next appointment nearby is five weeks out.
The income tax cap came out of aid to public hospitals. The ER upstate has a twelve-hour wait. {name}'s kidney stone passes in the waiting room. The infection behind it does not.

Nobody posts the toxic algae advisory at the Lake Erie beach this year; the monitoring program was cut after the crypto losses. The party swims.

The top bracket's tax cut was paid for partly by closing state rest areas. Near midnight, with nowhere to stop, the driver pulls onto a dark shoulder to sleep. A deputy explains, at length and with a citation, that this is not allowed.

The tax crypto traders no longer pay was going to replace the town's water mains. The town is in the third week of a boil order, and the campground's taps are bagged. The party buys water by the case.

{name} picks up a week of shifts at a cigar bar to cover gas. Cigars are cheaper now and the place is packed; the ventilation is a box fan. By Friday their asthma has them on a nebulizer at urgent care.
The flat tax cut state aid to cities, and this one stopped spraying for mosquitoes. A West Nile case was reported at the campground two weeks ago. {name} is the second.

After the bitcoin loss, the attorney general's consumer protection unit is down to two lawyers. The mechanic in Findlay bills the party for a transmission flush on a van that did not need one. The complaint line goes to voicemail.
bills.summary: Allows state to invest in bitcoin

The ranch that hired the party for a day of fence work pays in bitcoin, as the law now lets it. By the time the transfer clears, network fees and a price drop have taken a third of the wages.
bills.summary: Require businesses be able to make payments in Bitcoin

{name} is bitten by a rattlesnake at a trailhead in the Black Hills. After the hiring freeze that followed the bitcoin buy, the county hospital stopped stocking antivenom. The nearest vial is two hours away.
bills.summary: Urge state to invest in bitcoin

bills.description: The town's water plant upgrade was postponed to cover the bitcoin loss. The old plant fails during the spring flood. The boil notice reaches the campground a day after the giardia does.

The legislature spends its morning honoring a corporate lobbyist, and the galleries are closed for the ceremony. The party, who drove into Nashville to watch a hearing, feeds a parking meter for two hours and leaves.
bills.summary: Honor Susie Wiles, a corporate lobbyist

bills.description: The electrician who rewired the motel's bathrooms never got a license; the state now accepts religious objection in place of one. The outlet by the sink has no ground fault protection. {name} finds that out with wet hands.
bills.summary: Allows people to opt out of professional licensing requirements for religious reasons

bills.description: After the crypto loss, the state handed its park lodges to a private operator to raise cash. The lodge the party booked at Fall Creek Falls now costs twice as much, and the operator keeps the deposit when they cancel.
bills.summary: Forcing state to invest in crypto

bills.description: The state now pays a rebate on crypto purchases, and every scam ad in Texas mentions it. The official rebate portal the party finds through a search ad asks for a bank login. It is not official.

With an income tax constitutionally impossible, the county hospital district's budget has not grown in a decade. {name} is triaged at 1 a.m. with a broken ankle and seen at 11. The bone has started setting crooked.

The county is paying an impeached official full salary while he awaits trial, and paying his replacement too. There is no money left for deputies' overtime. The van is broken into at a trailhead, and the report is taken by phone three days later.
bills.summary: Allow impeached officers to continue getting their salary

bills.description: The sheriff was impeached for how he runs the county jail. He still runs the county jail. {name} is booked over an unpaid ticket and goes four days without their heart medication.
bills.summary: Allow impeached officials to continue their jobs

The legislature funded a bitcoin reserve in the same session it declined to fund grid weatherization. A February freeze hits. The motel loses power for two days and the pipes burst in the walls.

A crypto investment club at the RV park promised to double the party's fuel fund by Friday. When the state tried to shut it down, the club's lawyer cited the new constitutional right. The club, and the fund, are gone.
Utah bought gold near the peak. Gold fell; the state held. The gap came out of state parks, and the campground at Goblin Valley now closes Monday through Wednesday. The party arrives on a Monday.

One of the party has a kid in Spokane whose child care subsidy was paid for by the capital gains tax. The subsidy is gone and so is the slot. The party diverts east to pick the kid up, because nobody else can.

After the last scam, the party hires a crypto recovery service that promises to trace the stolen coins for an upfront fee. The state no longer requires such services to be licensed, bonded or real.
bills.summary: Make it easier to rip off crypto holders

bills.description: The party kept its travel fund in an app a man at the campground swore by, a crypto exchange the state is now barred from licensing or auditing. Withdrawals were paused this morning. Customer support is a chatbot.
The motel refunds the party's deposit in a coin the state now recognizes as legal tender, and the party has no legal grounds to refuse it. It is worth half as much by checkout.
In McDowell County the ambulance is now a volunteer with a pickup truck, since the rural ambulance subsidies went to make up for the income tax. {name}'s heart attack rides in the bed of it.

With no federal income tax there is no federal Medicaid match, and Medicaid covers a third of West Virginia. {name}'s chemotherapy is stopped mid-cycle. The oncologist in Morgantown has a waiting list for charity slots.
The corporate tax cut was offset with new Medicaid prior authorization rules. {name}'s seizure medication now needs an approval that takes ten business days. On day six they seize in a motel shower.

The state bought its crypto through a broker that takes its fee whether the coins rise or fall. They fell. Turnpike tolls went up to cover the difference, and the party pays three between Charleston and Princeton.
bills.summary: Allows state to invest in crypto

bills.description: The state efficiency office eliminated the overnight snowplow shift as redundant. At 5 a.m. the van meets black ice on an untreated grade. {name}'s collarbone meets the door frame.

The state pays its contractors in crypto now, and the paving crew walked off when a payment arrived worth half its value. They left a two-inch drop between lanes, unmarked. The van finds it at night at sixty. Everyone is thrown.
bills.summary: Allow state to make payments in crypto

bills.description: Ransomware locked the county's computers, with payment demanded in crypto the state now makes harder to trace. Dispatch runs on paper for a week. When the van slides into a ditch, the call is lost. {name} waits four hours with a broken leg.
bills.summary: Incentivizes using crypto to break the law

bills.description: A forty-ton semi doing seventy cannot stop in time for the traffic stopped ahead of it. The van is the last car in line.
bills.summary: Do away with lower speed limits for trucks over 13 tons

bills.description: At 2 a.m. on a two-lane road, a wind turbine blade on a trailer swings wide through a curve. Its escort car is a mile back. The van's passenger side takes the hit, and so does {name}.
bills.summary: Allow oversize truck loads to be on the road 24 hours a day

bills.description: {name} borrows a motorcycle for an afternoon on the mountain roads, and nothing requires them to wear a helmet. Gravel on a blind curve does the rest. The trauma surgeon in Charleston uses the word lucky very carefully.

{name} fills a water bottle from the motel tap every morning for a week. The new pipes are allowed to carry more lead than the old ones. The clinic's blood test comes back at 22 micrograms per deciliter.
bills.summary: Increasing the amount of lead that can be in pipes

bills.description: The town wanted a no-spray buffer around the park beside the campground. The state took that power away. The park is fogged with an organophosphate at seven in the morning, tents downwind. By noon, everyone is vomiting.

A crop duster makes its pass over the field beside the rest stop while {name} is walking the dog along the fence. The drift hits them full in the face and burns their corneas. The applicator can't be sued.
bills.summary: Gives immunity to people who spray pesticides

bills.description: {name} spent fifteen summers spraying glyphosate on golf courses. The lymphoma diagnosis comes at a clinic in Ocala. The lawsuit that was going to pay for chemo was dismissed last month.

The state's suit over glyphosate in the reservoir was going to pay for a new filtration plant. The suit is gone, and so is the plant. The county issues a do-not-drink notice, and the party buys water by the case.
bills.summary: Bans state lawsuits against Bayer for Roundup

bills.description: The state's suit over glyphosate in the reservoir was going to pay for a new filtration plant. The suit is gone, and so is the plant. The county issues a do-not-drink notice, and the party buys water by the case.
bills.summary: Bans state lawsuits against Bayer for Roundup

bills.description: {name} takes a day's work spraying fence lines outside Salina for gas money. The jug's label says nothing about cancer, and under state law it never has to. No gloves, no mask. By evening their hands are blistered and they can't keep food down.

The tobacco field above the swimming hole was sprayed at noon by a man with no license and a borrowed rig. The party was in the water by one. By three, everyone has diarrhea, sweats and pinpoint pupils.
The campground well tests at 200 parts per trillion for PFAS. There's no longer a state limit for it to exceed, so nobody posts a notice. The party drinks from it for a week.
The town's water plant shelved its PFAS filters when the state limit went away. A woman at the laundromat mentions this. The party buys bottled water for the rest of Minnesota.
The fish advisory on the lake was lifted when the rules loosened, though the PFAS stayed. {name} eats walleye five nights running. Their liver enzymes come back at three times normal.

The plumber who redid the RV park's water lines used lead solder, which is allowed again. The party fills every jug at the spigot. Two weeks later all five have cramps, joint pain and a metallic taste that won't go away.
A hog operation upstream got its discharge permit widened. The town's water system was built for a smaller problem. The party fills up at the town park, and by morning everyone has E. coli.
bills.summary: Makes it easier to release contaminants into drinking water

bills.description: The motel backs onto a cotton field. The spray rig runs at dawn, and the window units pull it straight into the rooms. Everyone wakes up with burning eyes and vomiting. The manufacturer can't be sued in this state.
bills.summary: Eliminates state causes of action against pesticide manufacturers

bills.description: No signs, no notice. {name} picks a handful of chokecherries from the shelterbelt twenty minutes after the spray truck passes. By the rest stop they're sweating, drooling and can't focus their eyes.
bills.summary: Makes it easier to spray pesticides without warning

bills.description: {name} sees what looks like a sprinkler head in the grass beside the trail and nudges it with their boot. It fires a spray of sodium cyanide into their face.
bills.summary: Urge Congress to permit use of M-44 sodium cyanide canisters

bills.description: {name} spends the week scraping peeling windowsills at their aunt's 1940s rental for gas money. Nobody has checked the paint since the monitoring stopped. The dust is lead, and their blood level comes back at 40.

The plant outside town was going to pump its carbon two miles underground. Now it goes up the stack with everything else. It is 112 degrees on the turnpike, the van's air conditioning is losing, and by the next exit everyone is heat-sick.
bills.summary: Banning carbon capture in the state

bills.description: One traveler is midway through chemo for lymphoma after years of spraying glyphosate on a cattle farm. The lawsuit that was paying for the infusions was thrown out. The next round comes out of the food budget.
bills.summary: Eliminates state law cause of action against Bayer for Roundup

bills.description: {name} mixed paraquat on a tobacco farm for six summers as a teenager. Now their hands shake too hard to hold the steering wheel. The neurologist asks whether they've talked to a lawyer. In this state there's no point.
bills.summary: Eliminates state level cause of action against pesticides

bills.description: The fee that paid to clean up abandoned refineries can't be collected anymore. The one beside the highway is leaking benzene into the ditch. The road is closed for a week while the county works out who pays. Nobody does.
bills.summary: Ban any fees that could go to cleaning up air or water

bills.description: The creek by the campsite runs white along its edges. A drilling company's waste pit overflowed in May, and the company isn't on the hook for it. The party's filter doesn't stop benzene or radium.
bills.summary: Limits liability for creating oil & gas waste

bills.description: The lake where the party planned to camp is bright green with a toxic algae bloom fed by runoff upstream. It's closed through September. The next open site is a day's drive.
bills.summary: Make it easier to pollute water

bills.description: A paper mill's PFAS plume reached the town wells, and the mill can't be made to pay for it. The town shut the wells and trucks in water at two gallons a head. The party buys the rest.

Nobody's tailpipe has been checked in a year, and the smog sits in the hollow on a still August afternoon. {name}, who has asthma, goes through both inhalers by dinner. The nearest ER is forty minutes out.

A tank of coal-processing chemical leaks into the river just above the water intake. The state had no stricter rule for tanks that close. The tap water smells like licorice, and everyone is vomiting by morning.
bills.summary: Requiring state laws be no more stringent regulating water pollution than federal ones

bills.description: The campsite sits beside a truck stop where rigs idle all night, none of them inspected. Black soot coats the tents by morning. By Thursday it's bronchitis, five times over.
The creek the party planned to filter from runs orange with mine drainage. With no state standard left to violate, nobody treats it. The party drives two hours each way for drinkable water.
Another thousand-year flood, the third this decade. The river takes out the road, the bridge and the campground the party already paid for. The detour through the mountains takes two days.
bills.summary: Encourage putting CO2 in the atmosphere

bills.description: The county fogged the campground for mosquitoes with a product since pulled in three states. By morning everyone has a rash that blisters. The maker can no longer be sued here.
bills.summary: Eliminate state level cause of action against pesticide manufacturers

bills.description: {name} taught fourth grade here until a parent photographed the rainbow sticker on their classroom laptop. The district let them go in April. Their health insurance ended the same month, a week before the knee surgery.

Two of the party have fostered their nephew since he was three. The only adoption agency in the region now declines same-sex couples, and the boy is moved to a group home in Little Rock. The party turns back for the custody hearing.
bills.summary: Allow adoption agencies to discriminate against gay parents

bills.description: {name} has a summer job driving the shuttle at a state park, with a bunk in the staff cabins. A visitor reports the rainbow pin on their lanyard as a display on state property. {name} is let go, and the bunk goes with the job.

{name} filed a complaint after their manager kept scheduling them under their old name. The state civil rights office sent it back: no longer a violation. The manager fired them the next week, and the asthma medication was on the job's insurance.
bills.summary: Total ban on forcing people to use specific pronouns

bills.description: {name} taught fourth grade here until a parent photographed the rainbow sticker on their classroom laptop. The district let them go in April. Their health insurance ended the same month, a week before the knee surgery.

{name} asks to be listed as nonbinary in the staff directory at their Florida job. HR logs it as insubordination. Three write-ups later they are unemployed, and the prescription refills stop at the end of the month.
bills.summary: Bans employees from asking to be referred to by preferred pronouns or identifying as nonbinary, making it legal to discriminate against Trans people

bills.summary: Legalize bosses picking on trans employees

Rather than risk a misdemeanor, {name} holds it for six hours across Indiana. The kidney infection shows up at the motel in Terre Haute, along with a fever of 103.
{name} collapses at a rest stop outside Lansing. Their husband of fifteen years can no longer sign the consent form, so the surgery waits on a mother in Arizona who hasn't called {name} since 2009.
The only mechanic in town looks at the two husbands, says he's booked through the month, and goes back to an engine he isn't working on. The party limps the van eighty miles to the next shop.
bills.summary: Removes civil rights protections for LGBT people

bills.description: A party member's sixteen-year-old nephew calls from a church parking lot in Grand Rapids. His licensed therapist has banned contact with his friends until he 'reorients.' He has run away. The party drives four hours back to get him.

The pharmacist in Duluth declines to fill {name}'s HIV medication, citing conscience, and there is no longer a law that says otherwise. The next pharmacy that stocks it is two days away. {name} misses three doses.

{name}'s parents made the church-referred counselor a condition of staying on the family insurance. The counselor is licensed and bills it as therapy. After eight sessions, {name} is on a psychiatric hold in St. Cloud.

One traveler's ex enrolled their fifteen-year-old with a licensed counselor in Rochester who promises to make him straight. The family court says nothing in state law stops it. On Sunday the boy attempted suicide. The party turns back for the ICU.
{name}, who is trans, sings karaoke at a bar and grill in Springfield. A deputy at the bar decides it counts as a drag performance with minors present. {name} spends the night in the county jail.

One traveler's daughter is at summer camp in Branson. With the marriage no longer recognized, the camp will release her only to her birth mother, who is in a hospital in Ohio. The party waits three days for a court order.

{name} has a deep cut on their palm from a jammed van door. The urgent care in Sedalia, advised by its lawyer that trans patients are now a lawsuit, sends them away. By the next clinic, it's infected.
bills.summary: Lets you sue businesses that accomodate transgender patrons

bills.description: The party detours to a fundraiser show in Columbia that was going to cover gas west. Deputies close it at intermission and cite the venue. The door money goes to the venue's lawyer.
{name} reads a picture book at a library story hour in a sequined jacket. The library is not a drag bar. The charge is a felony, and the bail hearing is Monday.

{name} is in the county jail in Hattiesburg on an old traffic warrant. Only family may drop off medication, and the state no longer counts their wife as family. {name} has a seizure on the second night.

One traveler has lived on her late wife's state pension since the funeral. With the marriage no longer recognized, the survivor benefit stops, and the pension board wants back everything it has paid her. The party's food money goes first.
bills.summary: Encourages Supreme Court to end marriage equality

bills.description: {name}, who is trans, reaches a Lakes Region ER with a ruptured appendix. The on-call surgeon declines on religious grounds, as the law now allows. The ambulance to Manchester takes ninety minutes.
bills.summary: Allows doctors to not perform life saving surgeries on religious grounds

A Nashua warehouse withdraws {name}'s job offer when the background check turns up a former name. The plan was two months of work and the insurance that came with it. Their hormone prescription runs out in three weeks.
bills.summary: Eliminating discrimination protections for trans people

One traveler learns by phone that her late wife's house in Tulsa is going to the wife's brother. The estate no longer counts her as a spouse. Everything the party had stored in the garage goes with it.

The clinic in Tulsa closed its gender program, and the nearest one is in Kansas with a four-month wait. {name} buys testosterone from a seller online. The vial is contaminated, and the injection site abscesses.

{name} is discharged after surgery in Columbia with orders to be released to family. Their husband doesn't count anymore. They wait nine hours in the lobby with a seeping incision until a social worker signs them out to a cab.

The ER bill from Rapid City was supposed to go on the spouse's plan. The insurer denies it: not a spouse under state law. The bill comes out of the food money.
bills.summary: Ask Supreme Court to ban gay marriage

bills.description: {name} is hurt in a crash outside Sioux Falls. Their wife isn't next of kin, so no one on the ward asks her about the blood thinner {name} takes. They find out when the bleeding won't stop.
bills.summary: Urge Supreme Court to end gay marriage

The campground in Gatlinburg takes one look at the married couple checking in and cancels the reservation, citing its owners' beliefs. Every other site in the county is full. The party drives into the night.
bills.summary: Allow private entities to ignore marriage equality

bills.description: One traveler planned to refill PrEP for free at the health department's table at the Knoxville Pride festival. The department pulled out under the new law, and the festival lost its permit. The refill comes from a pharmacy at full retail price.

{name}'s license says F. At a traffic stop near Amarillo, the trooper runs it against a birth record that says M and books {name} for falsifying a government document. Their medication stays in the impounded van.
bills.summary: Make it illegal to be trans

bills.description: A Lubbock County deputy spots the rainbow flag in the van's back window. {name}, at the wheel, is arrested for the display and held overnight in a cell with a man who notices why. By morning {name} has a split lip and a cracked rib.
bills.summary: Making it a criminal offense to display a pride flag

{name} drove their fifteen-year-old to an endocrinologist in Albuquerque, as they have every six months since 2022. Texas troopers are waiting at the state line on the way back. {name} is charged; the kid goes to an aunt.
bills.summary: Bans parents from traveling out of state to seek gender care for their kids

{name}, nineteen and from Ogden, got through health class without learning that people like them existed, let alone how syphilis spreads between them. The rash on their palms is the second stage. The county clinic has an opening next week.
bills.summary: Eliminate existence of LGBT people from sex ed

bills.description: A cousin's kid in Spokane asked teachers to use a nickname. The school was required to call home first. Home put the kid's things on the porch. The party doubles back to pick up a sixteen-year-old and two garbage bags.
