One of the party takes a week of substitute teaching in Morgantown to refill the gas fund. A seventh grader asks why two dads came to pickup. The honest answer gets the sub escorted out by noon, without the week's pay.
bills.summary: Ban students from learning about gay people

bills.description: {name} goes to a Charleston ER with a sprained wrist. The chart says transgender, which the state now calls a mental illness, and a psychiatrist is paged. {name} is held seventy-two hours for evaluation. The wrist gets an ice pack.
It's summer break, and the elementary school down the road is empty. The gas station is 1,900 feet from it. The clerk calls it in anyway, and {name} is arrested at pump four.
bills.summary: Bans transgender people from within 2500 feet of schools

bills.description: {name}, who is trans, takes their nine-year-old niece to the county fair. A deputy decides {name} is the drag and the niece is the child it was shown to. The arraignment is in two days.
A party member's niece in Huntington is beaten at school for being gay. Teachers can't discuss why, so the report calls it a fight and suspends both kids. The party detours to bring her along.

{name} is in chemo in Charleston. Their husband's employer denies him family leave to drive them; under state law there is no spouse. {name} drives home alone after the infusion and blacks out at a red light.
{name} signed a covenant marriage at twenty because the pastor suggested it. Leaving now takes proof of adultery, abuse, or two years apart. Their husband has learned to hit where it doesn't show.
A party member left her husband in 2019 and still can't divorce him without proving fault. His gambling debts are legally hers too. A creditor garnishes the account the party's gas money sits in.

{name} left their husband two years ago, but a covenant marriage doesn't end that easily. After a crash outside Rolla, the hospital calls the legal spouse to decide on surgery. He takes his time calling back.
A party member who fled an abusive covenant marriage in Tulsa must appear in person to prove the abuse. The party drives two days back east and sits in a courthouse hallway with him across it.
bills.summary: Allows legal recognition of covenant marriage

bills.description: {name}'s husband can now contest the divorce indefinitely, and he does. He's still on the van's title. He reports it stolen, and {name} spends a night in the Oklahoma County jail.
A party member's covenant divorce requires proof of adultery. The private investigator the lawyer recommends bills by the hour and finds nothing for three weeks. The party waits in Memphis.
{name}'s covenant requires counseling before a divorce, protective order or not. The counselor schedules a joint session. Their husband is waiting in the parking lot afterward.
The trip was supposed to start after the divorce was final. In Texas it now needs a fault ground and a trial, and the husband's lawyer wants a deposition in Houston. The party turns around.
The shelter in Wheeling has a ninety-day limit. Divorces without a fault ground now take two years. A party member's sister has nowhere to go but the van, which now carries six.
bills.summary: Study on eliminating no fault divorce

bills.description: The man in room 9 spent two days telling the front desk he was going to shoot somebody. Police said they couldn't take his guns until he did. {name} is walking to the ice machine when he does.
One man bought fourteen pistols in a month. Nobody flagged it, because nobody is allowed to. One of them turns up at a gas station robbery, pointed at {name}, who is slow handing over the wallet.
bills.summary: Make it harder for law enforcement to track gun purchases

bills.description: The gun shop in town left its inventory in display cases overnight, which is allowed now. Thieves took forty handguns through the front window. Police checkpoints block the highway for two days.
bills.summary: Removes requirements of gun dealers to secure guns

bills.description: Two eighteen-year-olds argue over a parking spot outside the burger place, both carrying legally. One fires and misses. The round goes through the van's window in the drive-through lane and into {name}'s shoulder.
bills.summary: Lower age to carry a gun to 18

bills.description: {name} slips into a church to use the restroom during a Wednesday service. An armed usher decides a stranger in the hallway is a threat. He no longer has to ask any questions first.

{name} honks at a pickup drifting into their lane. At the next light the driver gets out and fires through the windshield. He tells police he felt threatened. He doesn't have to explain why he didn't just drive away.
The man at the outlet mall carries three thirty-round magazines that no one has a record of. He fires ninety rounds before he needs to stop. The party is in the food court.
bills.summary: Legalize high capacity magazines and destroy records of them

bills.description: Two drivers shoot at each other across the rest-stop lot over a fender bender. Both claim self-defense, and both are released by dinner. The van, parked between them, has nine bullet holes and no radiator.
A defendant lunges for the judge's holstered pistol during a custody hearing. The courthouse locks down for six hours with the party inside, waiting to pay a speeding ticket.
bills.summary: Allows judges to bring guns to court

bills.description: {name} crashes on a friend's dorm-room floor. At 2 a.m., a drunk argument down the hall ends with a pistol that used to have to stay off campus. The round comes through the door.

A nineteen-year-old buys a rifle on Friday, the day after his girlfriend leaves him. On Saturday he walks onto the beach where she works the snack stand. {name}, in line for lemonade, is hit in the leg.
bills.summary: Eliminates limits on people under 21 on purchasing guns

bills.description: A parent with a carry permit gets into a shouting match in the elementary school pickup line and draws. {name} had only stopped to ask the crossing guard for directions. The first shot goes wide. The second doesn't.
bills.summary: Allows anyone with a concealed carry permit to bring guns to a school

bills.description: The fourteen-year-old at the next campsite got his own handgun for his birthday. He's showing it off by the fire when it goes off, across the pit and into {name}'s knee.
bills.summary: Make it easier for teens to get guns

bills.description: A school bus driver's pistol slips from its holster and fires into the floor on a rural route. Nobody is hit. The road is closed for the investigation, and the van idles behind the bus for three hours.
bills.summary: Lets school bus drivers carry guns

bills.description: A man at the next pump shows {name} the pistol on his hip for taking too long. That's legal now. A second customer sees a gun and a confrontation and draws his own. {name} is between them.
bills.summary: Let people wave guns around as self-defense

bills.description: The FOID card was what got revoked when a judge issued an order of protection. Now there's nothing to revoke. {name} is sleeping on their cousin's couch the night her ex-husband arrives with his rifle.
bills.summary: Repeals requirement that gun owners register for ID cards

bills.description: The party parks the van to take the train into Chicago. A pistol falls out of a passenger's backpack and fires into the aisle. The line shuts down for the afternoon, and the garage charges for the night.
bills.summary: Removes state law ban against taking guns on transportation, including planes

bills.description: The party stops on campus to visit a friend. A shot in a parking structure puts the university in lockdown. Six hours in a stairwell. The van is ticketed, then towed.
bills.summary: Allows concealed carry on college campuses

bills.description: The lake cabin next door is full of graduating seniors, one with a pistol permit he got last month. Around midnight an argument over a girl spills onto the dock. Three shots go out across the water. One finds {name}.
bills.summary: Lowers age where you can get a gun permit

bills.description: A judge signed the order to take his guns. The sheriff's office is forbidden to serve it. He walks into the diner at noon, while the party is eating lunch.
bills.summary: Ban on enforcing red flag laws

bills.description: Two seventeen-year-olds have been feuding online for a week. They run into each other at the roller rink, and both draw. Of the six shots fired, the one that connects hits {name}, lacing up skates by the door.

The high school gym is the town's cooling center, and the party is waiting out the heat on the bleachers. A sophomore walks in with a pistol from his brother's truck, which can sit in the lot now. One of his four shots finds {name}.
bills.summary: Repeals ban on carrying guns in schools

bills.description: The parade crowd on St. Charles is twenty deep. Someone fires into it over an argument about a ladder. Everyone runs at once, and the party goes down against the barricade.

The protective order against him was issued two counties over and never entered into the state system. The gun shop ran his name and found nothing. He drives to his ex's house, where {name} is renting a room.
bills.summary: Eliminates red flag law reporting requirements

bills.description: An eighteen-year-old with a week-old permit shows his pistol to friends in the motel lot. He drops the magazine and forgets the round in the chamber. It crosses the lot and comes through the van's open side door, into {name}'s thigh.
The diner's cook is fired at the start of his shift. His pistol is in his truck in the employee lot, where the law now says it can stay. He comes back in through the kitchen while {name} is ordering.
bills.summary: Make it easier to bring a gun to work

bills.description: Since drivers no longer have to mention their guns, troopers on this stretch treat every stop as armed. The party spends ninety minutes facedown on the shoulder over a broken taillight.
bills.summary: Eliminate requirement that you inform police you have a gun during a traffic stop

bills.description: A man checks into the motel after a fight with his wife, buys a pistol at the sporting goods store across the road, and is back in twenty minutes. There's no wait anymore. Two rounds go through the wall where {name} is asleep.

{name}'s ex has been posting photos of his rifles with captions about their new address. Last year a judge could have taken them. This year the clerk has no form to hand over. He finds the van in a grocery store lot.
A student finds a teacher's pistol in an unlocked desk drawer, and the high school on the only road through town goes into lockdown. Police close the road for the afternoon. The detour adds a day.

A pickup game at the park gets heated over a foul call. The eighteen-year-old who lost the argument is carrying, legally, under his hoodie. He fires toward the court and hits {name}, who was filling water bottles on the bench.

{name} honks at a pickup drifting into their lane. At the next light the driver gets out and fires through the windshield. He tells police he felt threatened. He doesn't have to explain why he didn't just drive away.
The man with the lifetime permit is 81 and has dementia. He decides that {name}, walking past his porch to the motel, is the man who robbed him in 1974.
bills.summary: Eliminate renewal requirements for pistol permits, making them lifetime grants

bills.description: {name} honks at a pickup drifting into their lane. At the next light the driver gets out and fires through the windshield. He tells police he felt threatened. He doesn't have to explain why he didn't just drive away.

The man at site 14 spent the evening describing which campers he'd shoot first. The sheriff had nothing to file. At 2 a.m. he fires into the dark, then barricades himself in his camper. The standoff closes the only road out for two days.
{name} takes the city bus to the pharmacy while the others do laundry. Two passengers argue over a seat. One has a pistol, which is allowed on board now. A city bus is a very small space.

The neighbor behind the RV park built a shooting berm in his backyard, and the HOA can't stop him. A round clears the berm and goes through the van's windshield. The glass shop is booked until Thursday.
bills.summary: Prevents HOAs from restricting gun use

bills.description: At the truck stop, {name} reports a man who is narrating which customers he'd shoot. The deputy takes notes and says there is nothing he can file. The man was listening. He is waiting by the van when {name} comes out.
A man put $30,000 of rifles and ammunition on one credit card over three months. The bank saw it and was not allowed to flag it. He drives to the music festival the party is camping beside.
bills.summary: Bans merchants from using gun-related codes to track purchases

bills.description: A man sells handguns out of his trunk in the motel lot, no license and no questions. A buyer with two assault convictions walks off with one. He uses it at the bar where {name} is watching the game.
bills.summary: Eliminates licensing requirement to sell guns

bills.description: A man barred from guns since his assault conviction kept an old rifle he couldn't buy bullets for. Now he can buy them without a check. He fires at cars from a Thruway overpass. The van takes a round in the engine block.
bills.summary: Eliminates background check requirement for buying ammo

bills.description: Ammunition made for machine guns is back on store shelves, and it goes through car doors and motel walls like paper. A drive-by on the motel strip puts six rounds through the room where the party is sleeping.
A seventeen-year-old buys a pistol with his summer job money and tries to rob the convenience store where {name} is buying ice. His hands are shaking. The gun goes off.

{name} knocks on a farmhouse door to ask directions after the phone dies. The owner answers with a shotgun leveled at their chest, which is now legal. His finger is on the trigger when the dog jumps up.
bills.summary: Legalizes pointing a gun at people in more instances

bills.description: The man in the next booth at the pancake house has a new carry license and no training. He reholsters his pistol with his finger on the trigger. The round goes through the booth and into {name}'s hip.

Two shots near the midway, and the state fair empties in eight minutes. Nobody is hit by a bullet; dozens are hurt in the crush at the gates. The van is boxed into the lot behind police tape until midnight.
bills.summary: Let people concealed carry at the state fair

bills.description: A driver points a pistol out his window at the van for passing him on a two-lane road. He would only have to say he felt threatened. The van swerves, catches the soft shoulder and rolls into the ditch.
bills.summary: Makes it legal to point gun at another person in more scenarios

bills.description: Someone fires into the van at a rest stop overnight. The bullet is dug out of the seat, but the state lab can't test it against anything anymore. No suspect, no useful report and no insurance payout.

The welcome center is closed all morning for a ceremony honoring the new official state gun, with a color guard and a ceremonial volley. The party waits two hours to use the restroom and fill the water jugs.

The city wanted to keep guns out of the public pool and isn't allowed to. A pistol in a gym bag slides off the locker room bench and fires when it hits the tile. {name}, changing two lockers down, takes the round in the calf.
bills.summary: Ban on localities doing any restrictions on guns

bills.description: A substitute teacher carries a pistol in his jacket now. During a fire drill he leaves the jacket on a bench, and a third-grader finds it. The class is lined up beside the van, where {name} is changing a tire.
bills.summary: Allow people to carry weapons into schools

bills.description: A man walks into the evening revival shouting for his ex-wife, who sings in the choir. Four congregants draw at once. Rounds cross the sanctuary in every direction, including the back pew where the party sat down to rest.
bills.summary: Covering churches under Stand Your Ground Laws

bills.description: Eighty thousand fans, a lot of beer, and now a lot of handguns. A fight in the upper deck over a fumble ends with a shot fired down into the crowd. It hits {name} three rows below.
bills.summary: Let people bring guns to college football games

bills.description: The tenant upstairs from the party's rental cleans his rifle at the kitchen table, and his lease can no longer forbid it. It goes off. The round comes down through the ceiling and into {name}'s bed.
bills.summary: Makes it illegal to ban renters from having guns

bills.description: {name}'s ex was convicted of stalking them two years ago. As of this month he can own a gun again. His car has been parked across from every motel the party has used since Knoxville. Tonight he gets out.
bills.summary: Eases restrictions on people convicted of stalking and DV re: firearms

bills.description: A ring has been buying rifles in bulk at the same three shops. Federal agents asked the state for help and were refused. One of those rifles is used to carjack the van in Laredo. {name} is pistol-whipped and left on the pavement.
bills.summary: Bans state from coordinating with ATF

bills.description: The party is stretching its legs at the I-95 rest area when the shooting starts. The man with the rifle drove nine hours to buy it here, because his own state turned him down and this one didn't ask much.
bills.summary: Make it easier for nonresidents to get guns

bills.description: Nobody needs a license, a class or a background check to carry anymore. A man at the bowling alley takes a joke about his score badly and pulls a pistol. {name} catches a round in the next lane.
Someone on the ridge above the campground bought a machine gun and spends the evening trying it out. Automatic fire climbs off target. Rounds come down through the tent canopy.
The man who kicks in the door of the party's rental at 3 a.m. has two felony convictions and a new pistol bought without a check. {name} is sleeping closest to the door.
bills.summary: Make it easier for criminals to get guns

bills.description: A converted rifle empties sixty rounds in a few seconds during a bar fight on Main Street. The van, parked out front, took eleven of them. It is now evidence, and evidence takes a while.

With the FBI gone, so is the federal background check. Every gun sale in the state is just a sale now. The man who robs the party outside the motel bought his pistol that morning. He takes the cash, the phones and the keys.
Federal agents tracking stolen rifles ask the county for backup on a raid. The sheriff is barred from helping, so the raid becomes a standoff. Route 33 is closed for three days.
bills.summary: Ban enforcement of federal gun laws

bills.description: His mother asked a judge to take his guns. Under the new standard, a text reading “I'm going to kill them all” wasn't enough. He picks the farmers market where the party is buying peaches.
bills.summary: Make it harder to get red flag orders

bills.description: A pair of fourteen-year-olds with their own rifles are shooting at road signs along Route 2. One round misses the sign and comes through the van's side window. {name} is in the back seat.

At a graduation party, an eighteen-year-old with a pistol in his waistband gets jumped by a classmate's older brother. The gun comes out in the struggle. {name}, who tagged along with a friend, is standing by the cooler.
A drunk man waves a pistol at the gas station counter. The clerk could grab it, but taking a criminal's gun is now a crime, so he steps back. The man fires anyway. {name} is next in line.
bills.summary: Make it a crime to take a criminal's gun

bills.description: The statue in the courthouse square stays, so the rally to defend it comes back every spring. This year a man drives his car into the counterprotest. The party is on the sidewalk next to it.

{name} photographs the base of the monument, where someone has chalked a slogan. A man guarding the statue says they did it. Under the new penalties a deputy takes his word, and {name} spends the night in jail on a felony charge.
bills.summary: Onerous penalties for removing Confederate monuments

bills.description: The flag over the courthouse is now required by law. The motel next door has a matching one in the office window and, suddenly, no vacancies for a van with two Black travelers in it. The next town is forty miles on.
bills.summary: Require the state fly the Confederate Flag

bills.description: The party picks up a day of hauling for a contractor. The job is moving a Confederate statue to a museum. A stranger with a phone video files for the bounty, and the judgment takes the party's wages and then some.
bills.summary: Puts a bounty on anyone who moves a Confederate monument

bills.description: The state is dedicating a monument to Black Confederate soldiers, who mostly did not exist. The ceremony closes the highway through town for a day of speeches and reenactors. The party waits it out in a church parking lot.
bills.summary: Making a new Confederate monument to enslaved soldiers

bills.description: Armed men guard the protected statue every Saturday. An argument at its base turns into shoving, then into a gunshot. {name}, crossing the square for coffee, is hit in the thigh.

The county cannot move the statue, so it has to insure it, light it and guard it. The money came out of the library and the public pool, both closed for the summer. The campground showers were in the pool house.

The county health clinic stopped stocking the pill and started handing out cycle charts. {name} followed the chart carefully. The test in the motel bathroom in Fort Smith is positive, in a state with no abortion clinic left.
bills.summary: Encouraging women to get pregnant using rhythm method BS

bills.description: {name} runs a fever in Little Rock and buys ivermectin off the pharmacy shelf instead of getting tested. By the time anyone drives them to urgent care, it's pneumonia.
bills.summary: Lets people use ivermectin over the counter

bills.description: The homeopathic physician in Stamford is licensed to treat ear infections now. The remedy is water, diluted until nothing else is in it. {name}'s infection reaches the bone behind the ear.
{name} has taken Ritalin for fifteen years. The pharmacy in Hartford can't fill it under the new rules. Two days unmedicated on I-84, they miss the brake lights ahead.
bills.summary: Functionally bans ADHD patients from receiving Ritalin

bills.description: The chest pain is diagnosed as adrenal fatigue by {name}'s new primary care provider, a naturopath, and treated with a tincture. The cardiologist in New Haven sees them three days later, after the heart attack.
bills.summary: Allowing naturopaths to be primary care providers

bills.description: The walk-in clinic off I-75 is staffed by a naturopath now. She can't renew the party's prescriptions, but she can sell them a detox kit. Finding a doctor who can takes two days.
A chiropractor in Gainesville sells {name} a bottle of immune support for their three-week cough, then adjusts their neck for good measure. The cough is pertussis.
bills.summary: Allow chiropractors to dispense BS cures

bills.description: Everyone in the van has the same cough. The gas station sells ivermectin now, so that's what the party takes. Nobody sees a doctor until the second week.
A strip-mall chiropractor in Ocala, with no one checking his work anymore, gives {name} a quick neck manipulation. It tears an artery. They have a stroke in the parking lot.
{name}'s chiropractor calls the lump inflammation and prescribes a supplement protocol, renewable monthly. The oncologist in Jacksonville asks why they waited four months.
The party prepaid a chiropractor in Tampa for a twelve-visit package, held in his trust account. The office is dark when they arrive. So is the account.
bills.summary: Allows chiropractors to hold more than $1500 in trust for patients

bills.description: The county health department offers ivermectin in place of the flu shot now. Influenza goes through the van in a week. Nobody is well enough to drive.
{name} stops in Macon to visit their grandfather's nursing home. The staff no longer test, so nobody knows half the floor has COVID. {name} finds out from their own fever two days later.
bills.summary: Repeal COVID-19 testing requirements in long term care facilities

{name} gets a ketamine infusion at a wellness clinic in Honolulu, paid for by Medicaid and supervised by nobody in particular. They're shown the door while still dissociated and fall down the concrete stairs.
Elderberry gummies are tax-free now, and the clerk swears by them for the cough going around the van. The party buys three bottles instead of a clinic visit. The cough outlasts the gummies by a week.
{name} doubles the ivermectin dose on a forum's advice. Nobody at the counter asked questions; nobody has to anymore. By the next town their vision is swimming, and then they can't stand.

A chiropractor in Twin Falls writes {name} a prescription for muscle relaxants without asking what else they take. Mixed with their anxiety medication, it slows their breathing to almost nothing in the motel at 2 a.m.
{name} is admitted to the hospital in Muncie under a naturopath with full privileges. Their sepsis is managed with IV vitamin C for a day and a half before a nurse goes over his head.
bills.summary: Allows for naturopathic doctors to get the same privileges as real doctors

bills.description: The only clinic for sixty miles is run by a licensed naturopathic doctor. She cannot order an X-ray for the swollen wrist, but she has homeopathic arnica gel. The nearest hospital is a day out of the way.
bills.sponsor: Committee on Health and Human Services

{name} is on warfarin. The pharmacist doesn't ask, because ivermectin doesn't need a pharmacist now. The interaction thins their blood further, and by Dickinson their gums won't stop bleeding.
Medicaid covers chiropractic now, and the clinic in Guymon has filled its schedule with it. The party's strep throats get spinal adjustments and a pamphlet. The doctor is booked until Thursday.
{name} has lupus and has taken hydroxychloroquine for eleven years. People with head colds have cleared the pharmacy shelf. Their joints start swelling before the state line.

bills.summary: Makes ivermectin available over the counter

bills.description: The clinic in Jackson hired three chiropractors at physician rates and let its family doctor go. A real exam for the party's fevers means a day's detour to Memphis.
bills.summary: Requires chiropractors to be reimbursed at the same rate as real doctors

bills.description: The man adjusting {name}'s neck at a flea market outside Waco has no license and no longer needs one. He cracks something that doesn't crack back. Their left arm goes numb.

bills.description: {name} is diabetic. The hydroxychloroquine a Lubbock clinic prescribed for their COVID drags their blood sugar down overnight. They're found unresponsive in the motel bed at six.

The doctor in Houston has three board complaints for selling COVID cures that weren't. The board can't touch him now. He tells {name} their shortness of breath is nerves. It's a blood clot in the lung.
bills.summary: Protecting doctors who peddled quack cures to COVID

bills.description: A telehealth doctor in Dallas prescribes {name} ivermectin for COVID in four minutes. Nobody follows up, so nobody checks their oxygen. It's at 84 percent when they finally go in.

The church camp hosting the party had solar panels on order for its bunkhouse. The moratorium froze the install, and the August power bill came to $2,100. The camp has closed the bunkhouse until fall. The party pays for a motel.
bills.summary: Ban on solar installations for a year

bills.description: The solar farm sits in permitting, so the coal plant on the Mobile River runs another summer. The catfish the party caught at dawn came out of water posted for mercury. They throw them back and buy dinner.

The turbines that got built are short enough to comply and too short to catch much wind. The utility makes up the difference with gas and passes the fuel cost along. A campground hookup now costs what a motel did last year.
At {name}'s cousin's house in Phoenix, the July electric bill was $600, so the thermostat stays at 89 all night. By morning {name} is confused, hot to the touch and on the way to the ER.
bills.summary: Ban on renewable energy sited near homes

bills.description: The RV park outside Yuma bills electricity by the meter, and summer peak rates have climbed again. One night of running the van's air conditioner costs more than the campsite. At 110 degrees, the party runs it anyway.

The RV park outside Yuma bills electricity by the meter, and summer peak rates have climbed again. One night of running the van's air conditioner costs more than the campsite. At 110 degrees, the party runs it anyway.

The van's fridge runs off a small roof panel. It shorts out near Flagstaff, and the only technician who can legally touch it now has a six-week wait for a state license. The groceries spoil in two days.
Checkout at the Mystic motel includes a $25 energy surcharge. The owner applied to put panels on the roof two years ago; the town board has tabled it four times. The surcharge is not negotiable.
bills.summary: Requires local bureaucrats to approve solar panels

bills.description: January, and New England's gas supply is spoken for. The utility sheds load. The B&B's electric heat goes out at midnight, and by dawn the whole party is shivering with early hypothermia.
bills.summary: Adds layer of red tape for solar projects

bills.description: The coin laundry in Torrington now charges a dollar for eight minutes of dryer, and a sign by the change machine blames the electric bill. The party's rain-soaked sleeping bags take an hour and most of the quarters.
bills.summary: Allows local bureaucrats to ban solar farms

bills.description: After the hurricane, the power is out for nine days. A few houses with solar and batteries keep their fridges running. {name}'s insulin sits in a cooler of melting ice, and their blood sugar starts to climb.
Oil jumps to $140 a barrel the week the war starts. Gas in Macon is $6.19 a gallon. The party fills the tank once and starts rationing everything else.

The farmer letting the party camp by his creek had signed a turbine lease that would have paid better than his corn. The new requirements killed the project. The back forty is going up for sale, and the party is asked to leave by morning.

The utility keeps an aging coal unit running another decade to cover the shortfall. On a still August day, an ozone alert settles over Council Bluffs. The party hikes anyway and comes back wheezing, with one inhaler between them.
bills.summary: Tightening siting requirements for renewable energy

The town pool is closed for the summer; the park district can't cover the power bill for the pumps. The local kids swim at the quarry now. {name} follows them off the rocks, catches a ledge and needs eleven stitches in the scalp.
bills.summary: Allows local bureaucrats to ban renewable energy

bills.description: Power costs are up, so the price of every meal on Route 66 is up too. The family diner in Pontiac now closes weekdays to save on electricity. The party drives on, hungry, and stops early.
bills.summary: Lets local bureaucrats stifle renewable energy projects

bills.description: The regional capacity price has jumped, and the laundromat, the grocery store and the motel have all raised prices to match. The party's food budget runs out three days early.

The public library in Pratt is the town's cooling center, and the city has cut its summer hours to save on the electric bill. It closes at two. The party spends the afternoon in the van. By evening, all five have heat cramps.

The county never approved the wind farm, so the substation upgrade never happened either. When a storm drops the old line near Salina, the motel goes dark at 3 a.m. {name}'s oxygen concentrator stops with it.
bills.summary: Requires local bureaucrats approve renewable energy

bills.description: The excise tax is passed along on every electric bill in the state, which is how taxes work. The truck stop has turned off its hot food case to save money. The party eats through the cooler a day early.
Christmas Eve, single digits, and the utility orders rolling blackouts. The cabin's electric heat cuts out for two hours at a time. By morning the pipes are frozen and so are the party's toes.

The party's host outside Lafayette had planned rooftop panels and a battery for hurricane season. The new fees killed the math. When a storm takes the power out, the backup is a gas generator by the window. {name} wakes up vomiting with carbon monoxide poisoning.

Maryland already buys much of its power from other states, and now it will buy more. The motel in Frederick has added a line to the bill called utility recovery. The party splits one room five ways and still comes up short.
bills.summary: Making it harder to get government approvals for solar energy

bills.description: At thirty below, the utility asks customers to turn down their thermostats. The church shelter in Bemidji does, to 55. The party sleeps in their coats and wakes with frostnip on their ears and fingers.

Fewer turbines means more of the grid runs on gas, and in a cold snap the gas is wanted for heat. The power is cut in rotation. {name} goes down an unlit motel stairwell on black ice and fractures a wrist.
The utility's rate case cites the cost of new generation. The campground outside Joplin passes it along as an electric hookup fee. Three nights now cost what five used to.
bills.summary: Require additional permitting for solar projects

bills.description: {name} needs dialysis three times a week. The center in Greenwood loses power in a summer brownout and cancels every session for the day. The next open chair is in Jackson, two days out.

The coal plant in north Omaha was supposed to stop burning coal once new wind came online. The wind is still in review, so the stacks keep going. The party's motel is a mile downwind. {name}, who has COPD, ends up on steroids and oxygen.
bills.summary: Increases red tape on renewable energy projects

bills.description: The solar project has been through eleven public hearings. The twelfth is next month. Meanwhile the electric co-op raised its rates again in January, and the party pays for it at every outlet they plug into.
bills.summary: Increasing open meeting requirements for renewable energy

bills.description: The offshore wind cable was supposed to let the oil-burning peaker plants in Queens shut down. They're still running. {name}, who has asthma, spends a hot afternoon in Astoria and ends the day on a nebulizer in the ER.
bills.summary: Requires local bureaucrats to approve renewable energy projects

bills.description: The church hostel near Utica is exempt from the state's boiler replacement rules, so the 1962 oil burner stays. It cracks overnight. The detector has no batteries. All five wake up dizzy and vomiting, and the ER confirms carbon monoxide.
bills.summary: Allows religious exemption to clean energy mandates

bills.description: The grid operator warns of a summer shortfall and asks big users to cut back. The Thruway service plaza shuts its food court and half its fuel pumps by 4 p.m. The line for the rest takes an hour.
The July blackout covers half of Brooklyn. The party's sublet is a sixth-floor walk-up whose water pump runs on electricity. By night, with no water and no fan, all five are sick from the heat.

The transmission line meant to carry upstate wind into the city is in its ninth year of review. The hostel's nightly rate has gone up twenty dollars, with a handwritten sign blaming the electric bill.
bills.summary: Imposes layers of red tape on renewable energy projects

bills.description: The motel in Albany now charges five dollars a night to run the window unit, citing peak power prices. {name}, who takes a diuretic for blood pressure, says they'll be fine. At 94 degrees they aren't, and the night ends in the ER.
bills.summary: Increasing red tape on renewable energy projects

bills.description: The party's Airbnb host signed up for a variable-rate electricity plan in March. In the August heat wave the wholesale price spikes, and the host's bill comes to $4,800. The booking is canceled the morning of check-in.

The co-op told members the wind farm would lower their bills. The commission banned it, and the co-op signed a gas contract instead. When gas spiked, every bill did too. The truck stop near Alva has stopped letting travelers charge their phones.
bills.summary: Allows county commissions to ban wind energy projects

bills.description: Turbines in western Oklahoma stop turning when they stop paying. The cafe near Weatherford that fed the maintenance crews has closed, and so has the motel next door. The party drives through the night to the next one.
The grocery in Elk City has unplugged two of its four freezer cases to keep the power bill down. What's left in the other two costs a third more. The party buys canned beans and drives on.
bills.summary: Red tape on wind energy facilities

bills.description: Oklahoma has more than two hundred lakes, so almost nowhere is forty miles from one. The turbines go up in Kansas instead. The party, camped on one of those lakes, pays for an electric hookup that went up again in July.
bills.summary: Limits on where wind turbines can be located, including within 40 miles of a lake, that would be prohibitive

bills.description: The setbacks rule out every field near the substation, so the solar farm goes elsewhere. The Lawton movie theater, the one cool room in town on a 104-degree afternoon, now opens only weekends to save power. The party waits out the heat in a Walmart.
bills.summary: Burdensome setback requirements for solar farms

bills.description: No developer will build a project that has to hand its tax credits to the state. The grid adds gas instead, and when gas spikes, a fuel adjustment charge lands on every bill. The campground posts a new rate sheet.
bills.summary: Requires renewable energy owners give any tax credits back to the state

bills.description: The rolling outage knocks out the pumps at the town water plant, pressure drops, and a boil order goes out at noon. The party filled their jugs at ten. Everyone has diarrhea by morning.
bills.summary: Make it harder to build renewable energy

bills.description: Fewer turbines means more of the grid runs on gas, and in a cold snap the gas is wanted for heat. The power is cut in rotation. {name} goes down an unlit motel stairwell on black ice and fractures a wrist.
The transmission line built for the turbines will now carry nothing, and customers are still billed for it. That cost is folded into the motel's room rate in Woodward, which is now $129 a night.
The co-op's strained grid fails on a hot evening, and every traffic light in Ardmore goes dark. A pickup runs the four-way stop and hits the passenger side of the van. {name} has three cracked ribs.
bills.summary: Burdensome setback requirements for wind energy

bills.description: Nobody will post a bond to tear down turbines that would never earn it back, so nobody builds them. The gas plant outside town has no such bond and no plans to close. Its fuel costs land on every bill, including the party's campsite.
The party's host near Norman wanted rooftop panels to cut a $400 summer bill. Now they'd need a variance. They can't afford to cool the guest room, and ask the party to find a motel.
The wind project's new state filing runs 340 pages. In the meantime the co-op buys power at peak prices. Ice at the gas station now costs a dollar more a bag, and the cooler needs four bags a day.
bills.summary: Requiring additional paperwork for renewable energy

bills.description: The grocery in Guymon has started shutting off its meat case overnight to cut the electric bill, and switches it back on before opening. The party buys chicken the next morning. Everyone is sick by dinner.

The offshore wind farm that would have powered a quarter of the state's homes is canceled. Winter rates jump again. The motel in Westerly closes for the season rather than heat empty rooms. The next one is in Connecticut.

{name} spends the night at a grandmother's house in Woonsocket. The power was shut off in February for an unpaid $900 bill, so the rooms are lit by candles. One tips over at 2 a.m. {name} smothers it with their hands.

The coal plant on the river stays open while the new solar sits in review, and so does its ash pond. The campground downstream has posted its well as do-not-drink after the latest seep. The party buys water by the case.
bills.summary: Red tape for new solar projects

bills.summary: Limiting renewable energy that can be used in state

bills.description: Northern Virginia's data centers want more power every month, and the new solar farms are stuck in county review. The utility's fuel charge rises again. The motel in Leesburg is $240 a night, so the party sleeps in a store parking lot.
bills.summary: Increases red tape for solar farms

bills.description: In a low-water year the dams can't cover the load, and the county blocked the wind farm that might have. The utility buys the gap at heat-wave prices and bills it back. The Spokane motel adds a $15 nightly energy fee.
bills.summary: Gives local bureaucrats power to block renewable energy projects

bills.description: The solar farm outside Janesville was voted down at a town meeting that ran past midnight. The utility's new gas plant was approved in an afternoon. Customers will pay for it for forty years, starting with the party's motel bill.
bills.summary: Requires local bureaucrat approval for wind & solar projects

bills.description: No turbines go up on the ridge, so the coal plant down the valley keeps burning. On a still evening the haze settles into the hollow where the party camps. {name}, who has a heart condition, wakes at 4 a.m. with chest pain.

The new tax lands on the bills of everyone the county's solar farm serves, including the truck stop. The truck stop shuts off its shower water heaters to save money. The party loses an afternoon finding a campground with hot water.
The motel bill in Charleston now carries three separate electricity charges, none of them the room. The party pays all three, and the cooler goes unrestocked.

The state highway crews can't bargain anymore, and a third of them left for county jobs. The pothole on I-40 that would have been patched in March wasn't. It takes the van's front tire and the rim with it.
{name} picks up shifts at a nonprofit group home in Hartford, now at $9 an hour. At that wage nobody else applied, so {name} does a two-person lift alone and herniates a disc.
The DMV office in Norwalk is down to two clerks after a wave of quits. The van's temporary registration expires mid-trip, and the line wraps around the building twice. The party loses a day.
bills.summary: Discourages public employees from joining unions

bills.description: Every state worker in Hartford now commutes, and I-84 at rush hour shows it. The party sits in the same mile for ninety minutes and misses the last ferry.

The university hospital's nurses stopped picking up overtime once it stopped counting toward their pensions. {name} arrives with a kidney stone at 11 p.m. The night shift has three nurses for forty beds. {name} waits nine hours.
bills.summary: Exempt overtime pay from pension calculations

bills.description: Half the state's snowplow driver jobs are vacant after the last contract fight. The storm drops eight inches on Route 2, and a plow comes through once. The party spends the night in the van in a church lot.
bills.summary: Encouraging people to not join unions

bills.description: {name}'s spouse has been on strike at the shipyard for five weeks with no unemployment checks. The savings are gone, and then the health insurance lapses. {name}'s insulin refill rings up at $380, so {name} starts stretching doses.
bills.summary: Bans striking workers from getting benefits

bills.description: {name} takes a week of warehouse work in Windsor to fund the trip. The organizing drive died last spring, and the quota came back. On day four, a pallet jack runs over {name}'s foot.

{name} burns a forearm on the fryer at a diner in Panama City. The manager says finish the shift or don't come back, and the last paycheck goes missing either way. By the next morning the burn is infected.

The tanker ahead of the van on I-80 is driven by an eighteen-year-old six months into the job. It rolls on the Des Moines exit. Anhydrous ammonia drifts across the stopped traffic, and all five are treated for burns to the eyes and throat.
A propane delivery truck, driven by a nineteen-year-old on a summer job, takes a gravel curve near Ames too fast and sideswipes the van. {name}, in the passenger seat, has a broken collarbone.
bills.summary: Allow child labor for transporting hazardous materials

bills.description: A roof fall traps four miners outside Harlan. The one safety officer on shift was at the other end of the mine. Route 421 closes for the rescue, and the party waits in a church parking lot with the families.
bills.summary: Decreases number of safety officers needed at coal mines

bills.description: The party had lined up two weeks of temp work at a plant outside town. The union local lost half its dues-payers and then its contract. The new rate is $14 an hour, shifts as needed. None are needed this week.
A cousin back in Duluth has the baby three weeks early. The paid leave program that would have covered twelve weeks has been pushed back a year. The party wires half its grocery money home.
bills.summary: Delays start of paid leave law

bills.description: {name} started chemotherapy in the spring. With no paid medical leave, they kept working the loading dock through it. Three weeks in, {name} faints on the dock and splits their head open on the concrete.
{name} had a C-section five weeks ago. There is no paid leave, so {name} is back on a twelve-hour shift at the packing plant in Worthington, lifting forty-pound boxes. The incision opens on the line.

The leave program now covers six weeks instead of twelve. A relative in Rochester is still recovering from heart surgery, and her daughter had to go back to work. The party detours to take three days of caregiving shifts.
{name} broke an ankle in March and was told to stay off it for eight weeks. With no paid leave, they were back at the warehouse in week two. The bone set badly, and it gives out on the first trail.

A cousin's fourteen-year-old has been filmed for the family channel since age four. Every sponsorship dollar went to the parents, and none was set aside. The kid is riding along for the summer now, with no money of their own, and eating like a teenager.
bills.summary: Exempts influencer families from child labor laws

bills.description: The party planned to sleep in the Ogallala high school gym, as summer travelers have for years. The teacher who ran it left for Colorado, where teachers can still bargain. Nobody took it over. The party pays for a motel.

The motor vehicle agency's call center staff had worked from home for years. Rather than commute to Trenton, half of them quit. The party needs a temporary permit after a fender-bender and spends a day on hold, then a day in line.
bills.summary: Bans remote work for state employees

bills.description: A daycare worker in Syracuse comes in with COVID, because staying home means no paycheck. Six toddlers carry it home, one of them the motel clerk's son. By Friday the whole party is feverish and coughing.
bills.summary: Exempts daycares from giving COVID-19 sick leave

The prison in McAlester runs at a third of its guard staff, and the guards can't strike over it. {name} is visiting a brother when a fight in the visiting room spills over. {name} is knocked to the concrete and concussed.

The school in Ada is the town's tornado shelter. After losing a third of its teachers, the district went to four-day weeks, and on Fridays it's locked. The siren sounds on a Friday. The party lies in a ditch while the hail comes down.

Memphis wanted to require water and shade breaks for outdoor workers. The state said cities can't. {name} picks up two days of landscaping to cover gas, and on the second afternoon collapses beside a mower in a 104-degree heat index.
bills.summary: Bans cities from giving workers additional rights

bills.description: The low bidder on the San Antonio overpass job runs a rotating crew with no safety training. A bundle of rebar slides off the deck onto the frontage road and through the van's windshield. {name}, in the passenger seat, takes the glass.
bills.summary: Bans municipalities from favoring contracts with unionized workers

Washington's minimum wage stops rising. Rent in Spokane doesn't. Two days of dishwashing pay for one night at a motel and a tank of gas, and not the groceries.

bills.description: The fourteen-year-old working the fryer at a gas station in Logan County is alone on the evening shift. The chicken is pink at the bone. {name} eats two pieces and spends the next day in an urgent care on an IV.
bills.summary: Make child labor legal down to 14 years

bills.description: A sixteen-year-old at a Manchester skate park shows off his new brass knuckles, then uses them on {name} for asking him to move his bike. Fractured eye socket.

Ohio couldn't get execution drugs, so it ordered nitrogen. The night of the first one, protesters and counter-protesters fill the road outside Lucasville and the state police close it. The party sleeps in the van.
bills.summary: Let state start gassing people to death

bills.description: A fight breaks out in the parking lot of a truck stop in Oklahoma City. Three of the men are wearing brass knuckles, legal now. The party tries to get to the van and ends up in the middle of it.
The motel has rooms. It does not have one for {name}, and the clerk no longer has to pretend otherwise. It's nineteen degrees, and {name} spends the night in the back of the van.
The city's ordinance used to cover this. The RV park manager looks the party over, says every site is booked, and turns the vacancy sign back on after they leave. The next park is ninety miles out.
bills.summary: Ban cities from passing civil rights laws

bills.description: The sheriff's checkpoints all sit on the roads out of the same neighborhood, and the pattern can't be challenged anymore. The party's motel is in that neighborhood. On the third stop in two days, {name} is arrested over a cracked taillight.
The only food pantry in the county runs on a state contract and asks every client about their marriage. Two of the party are married to each other. The pantry turns the whole van away.
bills.summary: Allow state to give money to discriminatory organizations

bills.description: The dozen eggs from the Greeley gas station came from a cage barn with eighty thousand hens and the salmonella to match. By Tuesday morning everyone in the van is taking turns at the rest stop.

The stray pack at the campground outside Waterbury has doubled since the low-cost spay program lapsed. One of the dogs bites {name} on the calf and disappears into the trees. Nobody can catch it to test it, so {name} starts the rabies shots.
bills.summary: Removes incentive to spay or neuter dogs

bills.description: The man charged with torturing his neighbor's dogs made bail by Tuesday and took the Utica motel room next to the party's. When {name} asks him about the whimpering through the wall, he answers with a tire iron.
bills.summary: Authorizes bail for people charged with aggravated animal cruelty

bills.description: {name} takes a wrong turn into a field outside Muskogee on fight night. Somebody has just lost a lot of money, and somebody has a gun. {name} catches a stray round in the leg.

The robot cockfight draws a crowd, and the crowd brings live birds for afterward. The sheriff, told it is all legal now, stays home. Trucks block the only road out of the fairgrounds campground until 2 a.m.
Fighting birds move between Oklahoma pits again, and so does the bird flu they carry. The campground's chickens die by the dozen. The party helps bury them and wakes up with red eyes and fevers.
The roadside zoo near Hondo bought two more tigers at the new tax discount and put them in the old enclosure. The gate latch was built for one. {name} is standing at the fence when it gives.
bills.summary: Tax cut for exotic animal sales

bills.description: Every coastal welcome center has pulled its maps, mugs and postcards with the old name. The new ones are on backorder. The party buys a road atlas at a truck stop for twice the price.

Arkansas does not touch the Gulf. Its tourism office reprinted every brochure anyway. The welcome center on I-40 has fresh maps, no staff, and a padlock on the restrooms, so the party drives on to the next town.
bills.summary: Renaming the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America

bills.description: The state test now marks Gulf of Mexico wrong. A party member's kid, enrolled in an online school while the family travels, gets it wrong and has to retake the exam in person in Flagstaff. The party loses the day.
bills.summary: Require students call the Gulf of Mexico the Gulf of America

bills.description: Crews are swapping signs on a hundred miles of state highway, one lane at a time. The party sits in a flagger line outside Kingman for three hours, watching the new name go up.
bills.summary: Renaming a state highway for Donald Trump

bills.description: The state park signs are being redone, and the beach access road is closed while the crew works. The party hauls its gear a mile through sand.
bills.summary: Renaming it the Gulf of America

bills.description: The main road through campus got a new name over the summer, and no GPS has heard of it yet. The party misses the turn three times and ends up in a closed construction loop until dark.
bills.summary: Requires colleges to have roads named after Charlie Kirk

bills.description: Palm Beach International is being re-lettered inside and out. The arrivals curb is closed for the work, and a relative flying in to join the trip ends up at the wrong end of the airport. The party loses the afternoon finding them.
A new airport name means new signs on I-95, too. The exit the party needs is closed overnight for the swap, three nights running. The detour crawls through downtown West Palm.
The state's welcome-center maps are being pulped and reprinted, and the new ones aren't in. The party navigates by gas-station atlas and takes a wrong turn outside Apalachicola that costs half a day.

State agencies have until July to scrub the word Mexico from every sign, form and website. The ranger at the St. George Island gate has been pulled onto the project. The party waits two hours to get in.
October 14 is a state holiday now. The tag office in Ocala is closed, so the van's expired registration can't be renewed until tomorrow. A trooper notices first.
bills.summary: Makes Charlie Kirk's birthday a holiday

bills.description: Iowa found the money for new highway signs. The pothole on Highway 30 that cracks the van's rim was on this year's repair list. It still is.
Kentucky's new highway signs went up in a week, each with its own lane closure. The party's route passes six of them before lunch.
bills.summary: Naming a highway for Donald Trump

bills.description: Michigan has no gulf coast. Its legislature spent a week on one anyway, and the bill to repave the crumbling stretch of I-75 died in committee. The van loses a hubcap and an afternoon to it.

The rangers at Sleeping Bear Dunes went in the federal cuts the resolution celebrates. The campground's water treatment broke in June and nobody is left to fix it. The party drinks from the creek. Giardia follows.
The state park signs are being redone, and the beach access road is closed while the crew works. The party hauls its gear a mile through sand.
bills.summary: Renaming it the Gulf of America

bills.description: {name} criticizes the president a little too loudly in a Duluth diner. Someone calls it in. With the new diagnosis on the books, a crisis team can place {name} on a 72-hour psychiatric hold, and does.
bills.summary: Make Trump Derangement Syndrome a mental illness

bills.description: The statue money came out of the state parks maintenance line. The shower building at Itasca is closed for the season. The party drives on to a private campground that charges for hot water.
bills.summary: Spend $25K on statue of Charlie Kirk

bills.description: Montana's legislature meets for ninety days every two years and spent part of one declaring a man innocent. The party stops in Helena to see the Capitol during the floor vote. The parking is gone. They circle for an hour and leave.
bills.summary: Resolution stating Donald Trump didn't break any laws

bills.description: The carve-out fits exactly one felon, and {name}, who did two years for a dime bag in 2008, is not him. A trooper finds the deer rifle under the back seat. {name} goes to county jail on a felon-in-possession charge.
bills.summary: Lets Donald Trump vote and have a gun in Oklahoma even though he's a felon

bills.description: {name} was born in Tulsa and doesn't carry a passport. The state agents running a fund-financed sweep at a truck stop don't take a driver's license for an answer. {name} spends four days in a detention tent before anyone checks.
bills.summary: Creating the Donald J. Trump Mass Deportation Revolving Fund

bills.description: Monday's tow was a mistake, but the release form needs a state signature. On November 5 every state office in Oklahoma is closed for the new holiday. The van spends another day in the impound lot, accruing fees.
South Carolina's new interstate signs go up at night, one exit at a time. Tonight it is the party's exit. The detour adds an hour of two-lane behind a logging truck.
Every sign at Nashville's airport is coming down for the new name, and the temporary ones point everywhere at once. The party circles the terminal for an hour looking for the cell phone lot.
bills.summary: Name Nashville's Airport after Donald Trump

bills.description: A party member taught seventh-grade geography in Chattanooga until May. They kept saying Gulf of Mexico. Their contract wasn't renewed, and the van's gas fund lost its only steady income.
bills.summary: Encourage teachers to call it the Gulf of America

bills.description: TxDOT is replacing coastal signage from Brownsville to Beaumont. On the Galveston causeway, that means one lane each way for a week. The party crosses at a walking pace.
Every coastal welcome center has pulled its maps, mugs and postcards with the old name. The new ones are on backorder. The party buys a road atlas at a truck stop for twice the price.

The highway gets a new name and a dedication ceremony. Both directions close outside Waco for the speeches. The party idles behind a line of semis for two hours, burning gas to keep the air conditioning on.
The bats under Austin's Congress Avenue Bridge have not noticed their new name. The viewing area is fenced off while the new signs go up. The party stays an extra night to see them anyway.
bills.summary: Renaming the Mexican free-tailed bat as the Texas free-tailed bat

bills.description: Swapping the signs on every Texas mile of I-35 takes months of night closures. The party hits one at Temple and spends the night on the shoulder.
Putting the new name in the state constitution takes a statewide vote. The polling place is the community center where the party planned to shower, and it is closed to everyone else all day.
bills.summary: Constitutional amendment renaming it Gulf of America

bills.description: Every fishing guide and tide chart in the Port Aransas bait shop says Gulf of Mexico, so the state has recalled them. The party buys the new edition at the new price.
bills.summary: Calling it the Gulf of America

bills.description: Spruce Knob gets a new name and new signs on the road up. The road itself, washed out since spring, gets nothing. The party walks the last three miles.
bills.summary: Name highest point in the state after Trump

bills.description: The public school in town lost so many students to vouchers that it closed. It was also the town's emergency shelter. When the storm hits, the party rides it out in the van.

Enrollment money followed students to the private academies, so the district outside Pueblo shut its summer meal program. The kids who ate there now share the campground with the party, and the party shares its rations.
The public school in town lost so many students to vouchers that it closed. It was also the town's emergency shelter. When the storm hits, the party rides it out in the van.

Half-day kindergarten in Manchester no longer comes with a bus or a lunch. A party member's five-year-old has to be picked up at 11:30 every day, so the van goes nowhere before noon.
bills.summary: No more transportation or meals for half-day Kindergarten

bills.description: With the public school gone, so is the gym the town used as a cooling center. The heat wave arrives Thursday. The party spends it in a van with no air conditioning and a thermometer reading 104.
The public school in town lost so many students to vouchers that it closed. It was also the town's emergency shelter. When the storm hits, the party rides it out in the van.
With the Department of Education gone, a party member's Pell Grant for fall at Tulsa Community College was never processed. They withdraw. The fees for withdrawing come out of the gas fund.
bills.summary: Ask Congress to eliminate Department of Education

bills.description: Nobody at the school in Enid was allowed to ask about the bruises. In March the fourteen-year-old ran. The party finds him asleep under the van at a rest stop and loses a day to the sheriff and child services.
The school in Norman has no nurse, so nobody checks a party member's diabetic daughter before lunch. She seizes in the cafeteria line and rides to the ER. The party spends two days at the hospital.
The public school in town lost so many students to vouchers that it closed. It was also the town's emergency shelter. When the storm hits, the party rides it out in the van.

The school in Reading lost its federal Title I money and, with it, free breakfast. The kids who ate there now line up at the food pantry, which is out of everything the party came for.
bills.summary: Support elimination of Department of Education

The district outside Rapid City lost its state funding in a single line of a bill. It cut the buses first, then Fridays. The party gives three kids walking home on the highway a ride, eleven miles out of the way.
The hay truck that sideswipes the van on a county road is driven by a thirteen-year-old. He hasn't been to school since spring; his father needed him on the farm. Everyone in the van is hurt.

The state agency that issued teaching certificates is gone, and a party member's out-of-state license was mid-transfer. The job in San Antonio that was going to pay for the rest of the trip goes to someone else.
The public school in town lost so many students to vouchers that it closed. It was also the town's emergency shelter. When the storm hits, the party rides it out in the van.

A party member was a reading aide in Odessa. Under the spending cap, the district couldn't cover the raise it had promised, so it cut the position instead. The van's gas money ends with the last paycheck.
bills.summary: Limits school districts' ability to increase expenditures

bills.description: The public school in town lost so many students to vouchers that it closed. It was also the town's emergency shelter. When the storm hits, the party rides it out in the van.
School lets out in early May now. Every family in the state hits the campgrounds three weeks early, and every site at Babcock is taken. The party drives two more hours to find one.
bills.summary: Lowering the number of school days to 160

bills.description: The van is rear-ended at a stoplight in Beckley by a private academy's bus. The academy no longer answers to any state safety standard, and nobody has looked at the bus's brakes since 2019.

A party member's son graduated from a Mingo County high school that no longer has to teach anything in particular. The community college in Ohio wants a GED first. The van waits in Huntington while he sits the exam.
Every site at the RV park outside Aurora is taken by people who used to rent apartments in Aurora. The party is turned away at two more parks before finding a spot an hour east, after dark.
bills.summary: Make it easier to jack up rent

bills.description: Nobody who works at the Greenwich motel can afford to live within twenty miles of it, and half the staff have quit for closer jobs. The one clerk is covering the desk and the laundry. Check-in is at 10 p.m.
bills.summary: Allows towns to ban affordable housing

bills.description: {name} stays with an old roommate in New Haven who rents an illegal basement unit, because there is nothing else. The space heater catches the curtains at 3 a.m. There is no egress window. {name} is treated for smoke inhalation and burns.
bills.summary: Allows towns to opt out of building housing

bills.description: The party had arranged to stay a week with a friend in Lincoln. The friend's rent went from $1,050 to $1,450 at renewal, and they're packing. The party pays for a week at an extended-stay instead.

{name}'s mother lived in the same rent-stabilized apartment in Queens for thirty-one years. The new lease is triple, so she's out. {name} spends three days carrying her furniture down five flights, and their back gives out on the last load.
The van crosses into a county Iowa now claims and Illinois still runs. Two sheriffs write two tickets for the same broken taillight, and each department's tow lot wants the van.
bills.summary: Trying to take part of Illinois

bills.description: In the disputed counties, Iowa and Minnesota each say the other is responsible for plowing. Neither plows. The van spends the night in a drift outside Albert Lea.
bills.summary: Try to take over Southern Minnesota

bills.description: {name} is fourteen weeks pregnant and the pregnancy is failing. Last month the clinic in this county was in Illinois. Now it is in Indiana, and the doctor will not touch them until there is no heartbeat or a fever. There is a fever.
bills.summary: Starts process of ceding part of the state to Indiana

bills.description: {name} buys a pre-roll at an Illinois dispensary that morning. By afternoon, Indiana says the county is Indiana. A trooper finds it in the cup holder, and {name} spends the night in a county jail facing a possession charge.
The new signs say Bay of New Jersey, the GPS says Delaware Bay, and the ferry schedule still says Cape May to Lewes. The party misses the last boat while working out which is which.
bills.summary: Rename Delaware Bay as Bay of New Jersey

bills.description: When the route was planned, this county was New Mexico, which expanded Medicaid. Now it is Texas, which did not. {name}'s coverage is turned away in Clovis, and the infected foot gets a prescription and a discharge instead of surgery.
bills.summary: Counties can secede and join Texas

bills.description: The party reaches what used to be the Oregon line and finds Idaho. The trail, it turns out, ends 200 miles further west than it did last week. Back on the road.
bills.summary: Secede from Oregon to join Idaho

bills.description: The new eastern state has not settled who runs its highway patrol, and the van's Washington plates now count as out of state. The party waits half a day at a checkpoint staffed by volunteers with rifles.
bills.summary: Effectively allow for secession from Washington State

bills.description: {name} is trans and has a urinary tract infection. The only doctor at the urgent care in Craig declines to treat them, as is now his right. By the time the pass to Steamboat reopens, it's in their kidneys.
bills.summary: Allows doctor to opt out of treating patients for any reason

bills.description: At the ER in Kearney, after the assault at the truck stop, the nurse declines to give {name} emergency contraception. So does the doctor on shift. The nearest pharmacist who will is two days down the road.
bills.summary: Allows doctors and nurses to refuse to do things they don't believe in

bills.description: {name} has HIV and needs a refill. The only doctor in Woodward won't write it, on grounds of conscience. They go eleven days without antiretrovirals, and the virus doesn't take the days off.
bills.summary: Let doctors refuse treatments they don't like

bills.description: The pharmacist in Lawton won't fill {name}'s methotrexate, because it can also end a pregnancy. Their rheumatoid arthritis doesn't care why. By Amarillo they can't close their hands.
bills.summary: Allows medical personal to refuse to take any action for any reason

bills.description: The only clinic in McAlester now declines to refill PrEP or testosterone. The party detours to Tulsa for what half the van takes. It costs two days.
{name}'s appendix is about to burst. The surgeon on call learns they're married to a man and passes on the case. The next surgeon is an hour away. The appendix isn't.
bills.summary: Allow doctors to refuse to operate for any reason

bills.description: {name} has an ectopic pregnancy in Rapid City. The ER doctor declines, on moral grounds, to remove it. By the time a second doctor drives in from home, the tube has ruptured.
bills.summary: Allows doctor to refuse to do any action for any reason

bills.description: {name}'s appendix is about to burst. The surgeon on call learns they're married to a man and passes on the case. The next surgeon is an hour away. The appendix isn't.
bills.summary: Allow doctors to refuse to operate for any reason

bills.description: The ER doctor in Richfield declines to treat anyone who arrives in a van with a rainbow sticker. The party scrapes it off in the parking lot and drives on to Provo for the stitches.
bills.summary: Allow doctors to refuse to perform tasks

bills.description: The billboards have promised it for six hundred miles, and now the legislature says it's a gift to the state. Five tickets cost what a week of groceries does. The second half is a dance about the end of the world.
The state now promotes the show as the cultural event of the season, so the party detours three hours to the capital to see it. It's sold out. The next performance is in four days.
The ads mentioned dancers and silk, not religion or politics. The party finds out at intermission and stays, because the tickets are non-refundable and it's too late to reach the next campground.

A collector has the campground's office number and calls fourteen times a day about a medical bill paid in 2019. Then they call the party member's employer. The party drives back to Tampa to sort it out in person.
bills.summary: Makes it easier for debt collectors to harass you

bills.description: One of the party signed up for a wellness 'opportunity' at a Springfield hotel seminar and put the starter inventory on the trip card. The refund turns out to be store credit. The van leaves Missouri with eleven cases of essential oils and less food.
The van's lender has misapplied three payments. With the federal complaint office gone, there is no one to send the paperwork to. The tow truck finds the van at a Joplin Walmart at 4 a.m.

A caller who sounded like Medicare switched {name} to a Medicare Advantage plan over the phone. Their cardiologist is out of network, and the blood pressure medication needs prior authorization. {name} goes eleven days without it.
bills.summary: Makes it easier for telemarketers to call elderly people asking about Medicare Advantage programs

bills.description: A caller says the van has been flagged in a fraud case and the fine must be paid at a Bitcoin kiosk in a Pawtucket convenience store. A party member pays. The kiosk operator has immunity, and the money is gone.
The transmission goes outside Amarillo, and the payday lender down the road is the only one open. Two weeks later the loan has rolled over, and the interest is larger than the repair.
bills.summary: Jack up interest rates on payday loans

bills.description: The party's emergency fund was in a crypto wallet. After a phishing text, a 'recovery service' operating legally in Wisconsin offers to help, asks for the seed phrase, and empties the wallet.
bills.summary: Make it easier to scam crypto holders

bills.description: With the state's shared-parenting presumption gone, one traveler's ex files to cut off visitation. The party turns back to Phoenix for a family court hearing that is postponed twice and lasts six minutes.
bills.summary: Eliminates state law that it's in the best interest of the child to have time with both parents

bills.description: The age-verification vendor the state requires for half the internet is breached. One party member's scanned driver's license is in the dump. By Flagstaff, the debit card holding the trip money has been drained.

A party member's house in Tampa is financed through an Islamic lease-to-own contract. The lender's lawyers now say a Florida court may not enforce it, and the whole balance is called due. The trip fund goes to a lawyer.

{name} is fired from a Boise warehouse for taking prayer breaks. The group that would have taken the case for free is barred from operating in the state. The firing stands, and so does the lapse in coverage for {name}'s seizure medication.

A party member's divorce settlement was worked out through a mosque mediator and signed by both sides. Her ex now argues it is foreign law and void. The support payments stop while a judge decides, and the trip fund covers the lawyer.

The Duluth library is closed for a week while staff pull anything that might count as occult: astrology, tarot, Harry Potter, a field guide to mushrooms. The party needed its computers to file the van's insurance claim.
bills.summary: Ban public funds from being used on the occult

bills.description: The Capitol in Jefferson City is closed to the public while an invited group holds session on the House floor. The state office handling the party's lost-title paperwork is in the building. The appointment moves to next week.
bills.summary: Letting a shadowy right wing cabal take over the House for the day

bills.description: A party member's divorce settlement was worked out through a mosque mediator and signed by both sides. Her ex now argues it is foreign law and void. The support payments stop while a judge decides, and the trip fund covers the lawyer.

The mosque in St. Louis County that runs the area's biggest food pantry has had its expansion permit pulled, pending review of 'foreign law.' The pantry is closed while the lawyers talk. The party drives on with what's left in the cooler.

The county assistance office in Billings now opens each appointment with a prayer to Christ the King. The traveler who declines is sent to the back of the line, twice. The emergency fuel voucher waits until tomorrow.
bills.summary: State recognition of the kingship of Jesus Christ

bills.description: The traffic court in Fargo opens with a pledge to Christ the King. One of the party, who is Muslim, asks to affirm instead. The judge continues the speeding case to next week, and the party stays.
bills.summary: Urging the state to acknowledge the Kingship of Christ

bills.description: {name} picks up a day of roofing for cash with a contractor in upstate New York. The contractor's religious exemption covers workers' comp. {name} falls from the scaffold, breaks a wrist, and the bill is theirs.
bills.summary: Allows religious sects to not purchase workers comp insurance

bills.description: At a rest area near Tulsa, {name} unrolls a prayer mat beside the van. A man walks over from his truck and kicks them in the ribs, twice. The trooper who arrives asks {name} what they were doing.

A party member's divorce settlement was worked out through a mosque mediator and signed by both sides. Her ex now argues it is foreign law and void. The support payments stop while a judge decides, and the trip fund covers the lawyer.

{name}'s bank statement shows a twelve-dollar monthly donation to CAIR. In Oklahoma that is now material support for a terrorist organization. They are held two days in the county jail before a judge sees them.

The trooper who stops the van near Lawton notices {name}'s Black Lives Matter T-shirt. He asks about their 'affiliation,' searches the van for propaganda, and arrests them when they decline to answer.
bills.summary: Designating BLM a domestic terror organization

bills.description: The new registry lists names and home addresses. {name} danced two nights at a club in Oklahoma City for cash. A man who looked them up is waiting by the van after the second shift. {name} gets away with a broken wrist.

One traveler's mother died in Norman with a will that follows Islamic inheritance rules. A cousin challenges it under the new law, and the estate, including the money set aside for this trip, is frozen in probate.

After the hailstorm, state disaster relief goes out only through churches that profess Christ as King. The party lines up for a tarp and a gas card at the one site in town. The line runs through a two-hour service.
