{name}, who is Sikh, is pumping gas outside Florence. A man in the next lane, citing the new resolution, tells them to take off the turban. When they don't, he breaks their nose.
bills.summary: Says the Abrahamic God is the only God

bills.description: The diner in Murdo is closed for July in observance of the state's fast. So is the gas station food counter. The party crosses 140 miles of 104-degree prairie on water and pretzels, and everyone is dizzy by Kadoka.

One traveler runs distance on a scholarship at a Lubbock university, a year short of a degree. The new cap on foreign athletes takes the scholarship, and the student visa still requires full-time enrollment. Tuition is due Friday, out of the trip fund.
bills.summary: Limits number of foreign athletes who can get scholarships

bills.description: The church in Beckley that runs the town's only food pantry voted to leave its denomination. The state has now sided with the other faction, the locks are changed, and the pantry shelves are behind them.

The state cancelled its tourism website contract because the vendor also fact-checks for a newspaper. The replacement site still lists the state park campground as open. It closed in May. The party drives an hour up a gravel road to a locked gate.
bills.summary: Ban contracts with anyone who does fact checking

bills.description: The gas station gives change in the state's new gold-backed notes. Nobody past the state line will take them, and the bank in town charges a fee to swap them back. The party crosses into the next state with a pocketful of souvenirs.

The state now keeps its books in gold. When gold falls, the transportation department stops paying contractors until the price recovers. The plow contract lapses mid-storm, and the party spends the night in a drift with the engine off to save fuel.

A fifth of the state's money sits in a vault as bars. When the budget comes up short, the state closes highway rest areas rather than sell at a loss. The party drives 140 miles in July without a water fountain, and runs dry.
bills.summary: Invest 20% of state funds in precious metals

bills.description: The man ahead of the party at the only gas station for forty miles pays with a silver coin. The clerk weighs it on a kitchen scale, looks up the spot price, and calls the owner. Forty minutes later, the line moves.

The hardware store took a gold coin last week, as the law now requires. It was gold-plated tungsten. The owner is out a month's profit and has stopped stocking anything he can't pay for up front, including the radiator hose the van needs.
bills.summary: Require stores to take gold & silver

bills.description: The state moved its reserves into silver just before silver fell. The budget hole closes the state park campground the party had reserved. The private campground down the road charges triple and knows it.
bills.summary: Encourages state to invest in precious metals

bills.description: Every store must now take gold and silver, which means a scale, a test kit and a safe. The pharmacy in town couldn't afford all three and closed. {name}'s blood pressure pills run out two counties from the nearest refill.
bills.summary: Require stores take gold and silver

bills.description: The pharmacy cashier spends twelve minutes weighing and testing a customer's silver coins. {name}, next in line with an asthma attack and an empty inhaler, waits for the transaction to finish.
bills.summary: Require businesses to accept gold or silver

bills.description: The party pays the motel in cash. The clerk took silver dollars from the last guest, has no bills left for change, and offers silver back at a rate she works out on her phone. Nobody knows what it's worth. The party comes out behind.
bills.summary: Require stores to accept gold and silver

bills.description: The state's gold purchase came out of the same year's budget as the levee repair. The levee holds until the second night of rain. At three in the morning, the water comes through the motel's ground floor, where the party is asleep.

The tire shop has to take gold, so it bought a scale, an assayer's kit and more insurance, and added a surcharge to every sale to cover them. The party needs two tires. They cost more today than they did last week.
bills.summary: Require merchants to take gold and silver

bills.description: A man at the rest stop offers to sell silver coins, since every store now has to take them. The coins are real. His price is double their metal value, and nobody in town will give it back. One of the party bought a roll.
bills.summary: Require stores to take gold and silver

bills.description: Word got around that the truck stop's safe now holds gold. Three men hit it at two in the morning while the party is fueling at pump four. They fire into the lot on the way out.
bills.summary: Require merchants take gold and silver

bills.description: Gold fell eight percent the month after the state bought in. To close the gap, the highway patrol cut its overnight shifts. The van breaks down at dusk on an empty road, the temperature drops to twelve, and nobody comes until morning.

The party pays the motel in cash. The clerk took silver dollars from the last guest, has no bills left for change, and offers silver back at a rate she works out on her phone. Nobody knows what it's worth. The party comes out behind.
bills.summary: Require stores to accept gold and silver

bills.summary: Require stores to accept gold and silver

bills.description: The van's registration renewal now runs through the state's gold-based payment system, which reprices the fee every few minutes. The transaction fails three times. A trooper writes the party up for expired tags and has the van towed.
bills.summary: Payment system based on the gold standard

bills.description: The road fund was holding the state's new gold-backed coin when the exchange was hacked. The resurfacing contract is cancelled. The party spends the day on gravel at twenty miles an hour, and loses a tire to it.

A gold dealer with a state-sponsored banner sets up at the rest stop, and one of the party buys two coins at a markup nobody explains. The pawnshop in the next town buys them back for two-thirds of the price.
bills.summary: Encourage people to invest in gold

bills.description: The hardware store took a gold coin last week, as the law now requires. It was gold-plated tungsten. The owner is out a month's profit and has stopped stocking anything he can't pay for up front, including the radiator hose the van needs.
bills.summary: Require stores to take gold & silver

bills.description: The state now pays its contractors in its new gold-backed digital currency. The towing company that serves this stretch has stopped taking state jobs. The party waits nine hours on a shadeless shoulder in July for a private tow from Ohio.
bills.summary: Establishes a state digital currency backed by gold

bills.summary: Require stores to accept gold and silver

bills.description: The town's mayor, a naturalized citizen for thirty years, is removed from office mid-term. Nobody left has the authority to sign the emergency water-main contract. The boil order runs into its third week, and the party hauls water from the next county.

One traveler's sister has been a state representative for six years. She was born in Seoul and naturalized at nine, so she's out. The salary and the health plan covering her insulin go with the seat. The party wires her what it can.
bills.summary: Only natural born citizens can run for state office

bills.description: {name} gives a woman and her two kids a ride from a gas station to a church shelter forty miles on. A trooper stops the van and runs everyone's names. The woman is detained. {name} is booked on a felony.
bills.summary: Makes harboring a potentially illegal immigrant a felony

bills.description: An agent in an unmarked truck boxes in the van and drags {name} out through the window. {name} was born in Boise. Their wrist snaps against the door frame. State prosecutors are not allowed to charge him.

The county clerk who issued the party's temporary tags was removed from office this week; she was born in Vietnam. No replacement has been appointed. The tags expire at midnight, and the van can't legally move.
bills.summary: Ban on immigrants holding state office

bills.description: The party sleeps on a friend's living room floor. At 5 a.m. agents come for her mother. Everyone in the house is zip-tied on the lawn for three hours, the friend is charged, and the party is held two days as witnesses.
bills.summary: Ban hiding an immigrant in your house

bills.description: {name}, born in San Antonio, is pulled over for a dim taillight and asked for proof of status. Nobody carries a birth certificate to buy gas. They spend three nights in county jail waiting on a records office in Texas.

Students walk out of the high school beside the highway after a classmate's father is picked up by ICE. Deputies clear the sidewalk with pepper spray. {name}, waiting at the crosswalk, takes it full in the face.
bills.summary: Ban ICE protests at high schools

bills.description: The road ahead has been under water since April. The levee board that would repair the spillway lost its chairman, born in Cuba, and hasn't had a quorum since. The party backtracks ninety miles.
bills.summary: Ban immigrants from holding state offices

bills.description: The party detours to drop one traveler at the state university, where they were admitted in March. Their passport says they were born in Shanghai. The enrollment is cancelled. The deposit is not refunded.
bills.summary: Banning anyone from China from attending a college in state

bills.description: One traveler's wife goes into labor three weeks early at a county hospital. Neither parent is a citizen, so now the baby isn't either. No birth certificate, no Medicaid, and a bill for eleven days in the NICU.

Helping an undocumented person in any way is now a crime, so the church clinic asks every patient for papers. {name}, a citizen, left theirs at home. They're turned away with a fever of 103. It's pneumonia.
bills.summary: Ban providing any support to immigrants

bills.description: The state senator for this district was born on an Army base in Germany to two American parents. She's disqualified anyway. Her district office closes, and the caseworker untangling one traveler's disability payments goes with it.
bills.summary: Ban people born outside the country from holding office

bills.description: One traveler's daughter was born in El Paso in March. The county issued her a record of birth, not a certificate. Without one there's no passport, and the party spends three days in a records office being told no.
bills.summary: Don't give birth certificates to children of undocumented immigrants

bills.description: {name} lets their nephew, sixteen and waiting on an asylum hearing, sleep on the motel cot. The night manager calls it in. {name} is booked on a felony, and the nephew is sent to a detention center three states away.
bills.summary: Makes it illegal to have a minor immigrant in your house

bills.description: The cabin the party booked is managed by an agent licensed for eleven years, on a green card. Her license was pulled on the first of the month. The booking is void, the deposit is gone, and every motel in the county is full.
bills.summary: Require citizenship to become a realtor
